In this study, an FTIR-based method was developed for the quantification of 2-phenyl-2-imidazoline (IMDZ), a corrosion inhibitor, and the influence of typical produced-water constituents on its spectroscopic response was investigated. Calibration curves were constructed using IMDZ concentrations ranging from 100 to 1000 ppm in Milli-Q water. Two characteristic spectral regions were evaluated, centered at approximately 1500 and 784 cm–1. The band at 1500 cm–1 exhibited a linear response with concentration (R2 = 0.9922), while the band at 784 cm–1 showed a logarithmic response. The estimated limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantification (LOQ) for the 1500 cm–1 band based on within-pellet repeatability were approximately 32 and 96 ppm, respectively. The effects of acetic acid, NaCl, CaCl2, FeCl2, NaHCO3, and dissolved CO2 were evaluated individually at a fixed IMDZ concentration of 500 ppm. Significant matrix effects were observed, particularly in the low-frequency spectral region. Acetic acid and FeCl2 produced the largest spectral perturbations, whereas NaCl caused substantial reductions in peak area. Overall, the 1500 cm–1 band exhibited greater resistance to interference than the 784 cm–1 band. Quantum-chemical calculations revealed strong hydrogen-bond formation between IMDZ and acetic acid, as well as cation−π interactions involving dissolved metal cations. The combined experimental and computational results demonstrate that the spectral region centered at approximately 1500 cm–1 is the most suitable analytical marker for FTIR-based quantification of IMDZ in brine environments.

item.title: Construction of a Dual-Response Fluorescent Probe for Potential Detection of Sulfites and NAD(P)H
item.description:
Abstract
Sulfites, which serve as significant multifunctional food additives, can act as potential pollutants or toxins in vivo when present in excess and can be reduced in association with NAD(P)H. While NAD(P)H is a central redox coenzyme that fuels mitochondrial ATP production, sustains cellular redox balance, and regulates diverse signaling pathways, it would be invaluable to monitor the rapid subcellular fluctuations of NAD(P)H and sulfites for a comprehensive understanding of metabolic syndromes, neurodegenerative disorders, and ischemia-related injuries by constructing a dual-response fluorescent probe. Herein, FL-D was designed and synthesized as an excitation-gated dual-response fluorescent probe that decouples the optical detection of sulfites from cellular reducing power within a single molecular scaffold. Built on a functionalized quinolinium platform, FL-D exhibited spectroscopically orthogonal response modes governed by the excitation wavelength. Under 378 nm excitation, FL-D functioned as a ratiometric sensor for bisulfite and sulfite (HSO3–/SO32–), utilizing intrinsic emission bands at 434 and 510 nm to display a pronounced ratiometric shift with high selectivity against competing biothiols. In contrast, under 500 nm excitation, FL-D entirely bypassed the sulfur-responsive spectral window, operating as a specific turn-on fluorescent reporter for NADH and generating a strong emission enhancement at 577 nm under physiological conditions (up to 100-fold variation), which could potentially monitor fluctuations in NADH and sulfites. Such profound excitation-gated orthogonality should enable independent yet simultaneous interrogation of sulfur metabolism and nicotinamide redox status without reliance on probe cocktails or complex spectral unmixing for further investigation.

item.title: Effect of Guanidine Carbonate on the Optical Properties of KClO 3 –Lactose-Based Orange Smoke-Generating Composition
item.description:
Abstract
To investigate the influence of the nitrogen-rich additive guanidine carbonate (GC) on the optical performance of orange-colored smoke compositions, pyrotechnic formulations with varying GC contents were evaluated using a self-made sealed smoke chamber. A stroboscopic spectrum analyzer and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) were employed to characterize the optical properties of smoke aerosol and compositions of combustion residue and thus elucidate the mechanism by which GC modulates the optical performance of KClO3–lactose-based orange-colored smoke compositions. The results showed that at GC contents of 0–4 wt %, the aerosol exhibited low broadband transmittance, with ΔT suppressed to approximately 1.45%. At a GC content of 8–12 wt %, the early endothermic decomposition and gas evolution of GC eliminate the high-temperature exothermic stage of the system and shorten the time the dye resides in the high-temperature region, which is hypothesized to minimize the thermal degradation of the dye during vaporization. Consequently, ΔT increased sharply to 8.06–8.34%, yielding orange-colored smoke compositions with high color rendering purity. However, at a GC content of 16 wt %, excessive endothermic cooling caused thermal quenching and interrupted combustion, and FTIR confirmed that the characteristic peaks of the dye were retained in the residue. Overall, a GC content of 8–12 wt % provided the optimal balance between thermal regulation and dye sublimation, offering a quantitative basis for the formulation and design of orange-smoke agents with high colorimetric purity.

item.title: Trivalent-Conjugated-Cation Layered Lead Chloride (Tptz)Pb 2 Cl 7 : Crystal Structure, Electronic Properties, and Photodetection
item.description:
Abstract
Two-dimensional (2D) layered perovskites offer a versatile platform for exploring hybrid halides with tunable optoelectronic properties, owing to their structural diversity and enhanced interlayer coupling. Herein, we report a novel Pb-based 2D layered perovskite (Tptz)Pb2Cl7 (Tptz = 2,4,6-tri(4-pyridyl)-1,3,5-triazine), in which trivalent conjugated Tptz3+ cations are incorporated into this structural family. Single-crystal structure analysis reveals that its structural connectivity resembles the [H3tib]Pb2Br7-type architecture, and DFT calculations further show that strong C–H...Cl hydrogen bonds between the [Pb2Cl7]3– framework and Tptz3+ cations facilitate efficient interlayer carrier transport. More intriguingly, the conjugated cations directly contribute to the band structure, inducing anomalous bandgap narrowing that extends the absorption edge into the visible region, as evidenced by the deep-yellow crystal color. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the (Tptz)Pb2Cl7 single-crystal photodetector achieves an outstanding on/off ratio of 1.71 × 104, a linear dynamic range (LDR) of 101.83, and a specific detectivity (D*) of 8.02 × 1010 Jones, comparable to those of state-of-the-art Br/I-based perovskite single-crystal devices. Moreover, the device exhibits self-powered photoresponse to X-ray irradiation at 0 V, highlighting its potential for low-power radiation detection.

item.title: Torrefaction-Assisted Fractionation of Material Recovery Facility Waste
item.description:
Abstract
Material recovery facility (MRF) residues are heterogeneous mixtures of plastics, paper/cardboard, and mineral matter that are difficult to separate and are commonly landfilled. This study evaluated whether torrefaction-induced changes in grindability can enable size-based enrichment of plastic-, biogenic-, and mineral-rich components from MRF-derived municipal solid waste (MRF-MSW). Approximately 150 g batches were torrefied at 300–400 °C for 5–150 min, producing 0–55% mass loss, and then ground and vibro-sifted into >850, 74–850, and <74 μm fractions. Across the investigated torrefaction severities, 60–80% of the recovered ash was concentrated in the <74 μm fraction, whereas the >850 μm fraction at low mass loss had the highest higher heating value (HHV) and was enriched in plastics. Microscopy and elemental analysis revealed that the materials were concentrated into plastic, biogenic, and mineral-rich fractions. Above approximately 20% mass loss, all retained material passed the 850 μm screen. The chlorine contribution from the coarse plastic-rich fraction declined to essentially zero above approximately 25% mass loss, while most residual chlorine was associated with the mineral-rich fine fraction. These results show that torrefaction severity can be adjusted to control grindability and facilitate physical fractionation of heterogeneous MRF-MSW.

item.title: Fruit Quality of Tomato Plants Grown under Deficit Irrigation and Treated with Nano-Oxides, Mineral Salts, and Bioinoculants
item.description:
Abstract
Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) fruit quality may be affected by deficit irrigation and by Fe, Zn, and microbial inputs. This study evaluated fruit-quality attributes at harvest in HM 2798 tomato under full and deficit irrigation. The experiment was conducted in a 6 × 2 factorial arrangement in a randomized complete block design with four blocks, comprising six treatments and two irrigation regimes, for a total of 48 experimental units. The treatments consisted of a control, ZnO and Fe2O3 nano-oxides, ZnSO4·7H2O and FeSO4·7H2O conventional salts, and a combined commercial bioinoculant treatment (Azokop + No-Nema) applied to the root zone, evaluated under full irrigation (100% crop evapotranspiration, ETc) and deficit irrigation (50% ETc). The Fe and Zn sources were sprayed on the foliage at nonequivalent elemental doses, with the conventional salts supplying approximately five times more Fe or Zn than the nano-oxides. Fruits were harvested once at the USDA Red stage (>90% red surface), and physicochemical attributes, soluble sugars, ascorbic acid, pigments, flavonoids, anthocyanins, and phenolic compounds were evaluated. Under 50% ETc, FeSO4·7H2O resulted in the highest total soluble, reducing, and nonreducing sugar contents, reaching 7.04, 1.23, and 5.81 g 100 g–1 FW, respectively, corresponding to increases of 64.4, 163.2, and 52.3% relative to the control. NPZnO resulted in the highest flavonoid content under 100% ETc (2.47 mg 100 g–1 FW; +27.7% relative to the control). The combined commercial bioinoculant treatment resulted in carotenoid contents of 13.09 and 12.28 mg 100 g–1 FW under 100% and 50% ETc, respectively, with no significant difference between irrigation regimes. ZnSO4·7H2O resulted in the highest phenolic compound content under 100% ETc (32.50 mg GAE 100 g–1 FW; +70.0% relative to the control). Overall, the responses depended on both treatment and irrigation regime, demonstrating specific changes in tomato fruit composition at harvest rather than a uniform mitigation effect of nano-oxides, conventional salts, or bioinoculants. Because dose, formulation, and, for the bioinoculants, application route differed among treatments, these results characterize the specific treatment programs tested rather than the intrinsic efficiency of nano or conventional formulations.

item.title: Preferential Freeze–Thaw Damage in Limestone Containing Stylolites and Calcite Veins from High-Altitude Mining Areas
item.description:
Abstract
Limestone slopes in high-altitude mining areas are subjected to strong diurnal temperature fluctuations and repeated freeze–thaw cycles, which can induce the development of internal pores and cracks and cause structural deterioration of the rock mass. However, where preferential damage occurs and how it affects the structural continuity of limestone remain unclear. To investigate how structural units, including stylolites, calcite veins, and the matrix, control the spatial distribution of freeze–thaw damage in natural limestone, this study examined limestone containing stylolites and calcite veins. The specimens were classified into sparse and dense structural-unit types according to the degree of structural-unit development. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance T2 spectra, magnetic resonance imaging, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive spectroscopy, and P-wave velocity tests were combined to reveal the evolution of the pore structure, microscopic damage, and structural continuity under freeze–thaw cycles. The results show that the dense structural-unit specimens exhibited a more pronounced increase in long-T2 components, clustering of high-signal MRI regions, and P-wave velocity attenuation. After 30 freeze–thaw cycles, the velocity attenuation rate of the dense specimens reached 28–30%, significantly higher than that of the sparse specimens, which was 10–12%. The absolute value of the fitted porosity–velocity slope for the dense specimens was approximately 2.17 times that of the sparse specimens. SEM-EDS results indicate that the matrix and calcite vein interiors showed limited changes, although localized crack-like features developed near some vein boundaries after 30 cycles, whereas stylolites gradually evolved into widened, deepened, and rough-bounded banded damage zones, accompanied by relative Ca depletion and local enrichment of Si and Al. These findings demonstrate that freeze–thaw damage in natural limestone is not a uniform accumulation process but a stylolite-dominated preferential damage process controlled by mineralogical-structural heterogeneity. This understanding provides experimental evidence for identifying freeze–thaw damage characteristics and determining key monitoring zones of limestone slopes containing natural structural units in high-altitude mining areas.

item.title: Synthesis of Fused Biimidazole-Containing Polymers and Their Application as High-Potential Organic Cathode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Abstract
The development of sustainable cathode-active materials for lithium-ion batteries requires organic redox systems that combine high reaction potential, sufficient capacity, and cycling stability. High-potential n-type redox-active motifs are particularly attractive because smaller-sized cation insertion generally enables smoother ion diffusion than in p-type systems; however, such materials remain limited. In this study, we report the synthesis of a fused biimidazole-containing polymer, poly(biimidazo[4,5-b]-1,4-benzoquinone) (PBIBQ), and investigate its applicability as a high-potential organic cathode material. PBIBQ was synthesized from tetraamino-1,4-benzoquinone and oxalic acid, and its structure was characterized by solid-state NMR and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Electrochemical measurements revealed that PBIBQ exhibits reversible redox behavior with an average discharge potential of 3.25 V vs Li/Li+ and a specific capacity of 133 mAh g–1, demonstrating one of the highest energy-density levels among nonbenzoquinone/hydroquinone-type organic cathodes. Ex situ XPS analyses and density functional theory calculations support that the biimidazole/tetraazafulvalene-type unit functions as the redox-active center and suggest that Li+ insertion between nitrogen atoms is the dominant charge-storage process. However, PBIBQ suffered a gradual capacity decrease during multicycling due to dissolution of the active material and/or its reduced derivatives. To address this issue, a cross-linked derivative, NW-PBIBQ, was synthesized using a tetrafunctional carboxylic acid linker, and the composite of NW-PBIBQ and multiwalled carbon nanotubes was further prepared to improve charge transport. These approaches successfully suppressed dissolution and lowered charge-transfer resistance, improving rate capability and cycle stability. Overall, these results demonstrate that a fused biimidazole-based polymer is a promising molecular motif to realize high-voltage n-type organic cathode.

item.title: Ultrasound-Assisted Enzymatic Extraction of Flavonoids from Pouteria caimito Leaves: Process Optimization, Mechanistic Investigation, and Bioactivity Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
To enhance the resource utilization value of Pouteria caimito leaves, this study employed ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction (UAE) to extract flavonoids from Pouteria caimito leaves (PCL). The UAE process was optimized using single-factor experiments combined with response surface methodology. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) were used to investigate structural changes in leaf tissues and the synergistic extraction effects of ultrasound and enzymatic hydrolysis. UHPLC-HRMS/MS was used to characterize extracts obtained by different extraction methods, and seasonal variations in flavonoid content and biological activity were also evaluated. The optimal extraction conditions were as follows: solid–liquid ratio of 1:50, ethanol concentration of 50%, pH 3.6, enzyme addition of 1.6%, enzymatic hydrolysis temperature of 50 °C, enzymatic hydrolysis time of 51 min, ultrasonic temperature of 50 °C, and ultrasonic time of 39 min. Under these conditions, the flavonoid extraction yield by UAE was higher than that achieved by ultrasonic extraction (UE) or enzymatic extraction (EE) alone. SEM, FT-IR, and XRD results demonstrated more extensive cell wall disruption and higher extraction efficiency with UAE. After purification using AB-8 macroporous resin, flavonoid purity increased from 32.84% to 73.15%. Activity evaluation showed that the purified product (MRP) exhibited strong antioxidant and multienzyme inhibitory activities: DPPH IC50 = (0.0197 ± 0.0014) mg/mL, ABTS+• IC50 = (0.0560 ± 0.0016) mg/mL, tyrosinase IC50 = (0.2911 ± 0.0022) mg/mL, acetylcholinesterase IC50 = (0.5303 ± 0.0101) mg/mL, and α-amylase IC50 = (0.3328 ± 0.0100) mg/mL. Network pharmacology further identified catechin, dihydrotricetin, and kaempferol 3,5,7-trimethyl ether as key candidate compounds and suggested that their potential effects against Alzheimer’s disease may involve AChE-related regulation within the “Neuroactive ligand signaling” pathway. January was identified as the optimal harvest period. This study demonstrates the potential of UAE for the high-value utilization of PCL flavonoids.

item.title: Provenance, Depositional Facies and Favorable Reservoir Distribution of the Lower Cretaceous Yageliemu Formation in the Kuqa Depression, Tarim Basin, NW China
item.description:
Abstract
Tectonic movements and related depositional responses are always complicated in a typical foreland basin. This study investigates the provenance and depositional facies of the Cretaceous Yageliemu Formation in the Kuqa Depression, Tarim Basin, NW China, to determine favorable reservoir distribution. Evidence from detrital zircon U–Pb age and heavy mineral assemblages illustrates two mainly provenances: (1) the Kelasu River characterized by the U–Pb age from 220 to 400 Ma and 420 to 560 Ma and the heavy mineral assemblages of leucoxene, zircon, and barite; (2) the Kuqa River dominated by the U–Pb age from 300 to 520 Ma and the heavy mineral assemblages of barite and apatite. Integration of core, well logging curves, and seismic responses indicates that the Yageliemu Formation can be subdivided into three parasequence sets: EL2, EL1, and LL1. The parasequence sets of EL2 and EL1 are favorable for the development and accumulation of large-scale sand bodies. The sediments in the Yageliemu Formation mainly consist of pebbly sandstone, coarse- to fine-grained sandstone, siltstone, and silty mudstone deposited in a braided-river delta front setting. The braided-river delta front subfacies can be divided into subaqueous distributary channels, proximal mouth bar, and distal mouth bar microfacies. Based on paleogeomorphology reconstruction, seismic attribute facies and core observations, depositional facies and distribution of favorable reservoir facies in the EL1 and EL2 intervals is predicted. This study innovatively identifies two distinct provenance systems, establishes a high-resolution sequence stratigraphic framework, reconstructs the source-to-sink paleogeomorphic configuration, and proposes a hierarchical favorable reservoir prediction model for the Yageliemu Formation. It deepens insights into sedimentary responses of compressional foreland basins and guides ultradeep tight gas exploration in the Kuqa Depression.

item.title: A Previously Unreported Octapeptide from Ganoderma lucidum Attenuates Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in LPS-Stimulated Macrophages via Modulation of NF-κB and COX-2 Signaling
item.description:
Abstract
Ganoderma lucidum is a source of bioactive peptides with reported immunomodulatory properties. In this study, an octapeptide, TNFSNCTL, was identified from G. lucidum hydrolyzates using de novo sequencing coupled with LC–MS/MS and subsequently synthesized via solid-phase peptide synthesis. Querying both the NCBI nonredundant (NR) database and G. lucidum protein sequences returned no exact contiguous alignment, suggesting that TNFSNCTL has not been described before. Its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties were then characterized in cell-free systems and in RAW264.7 macrophages challenged with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Treatment lowered the intracellular levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and nitric oxide (NO) while remaining minimally toxic to fibroblasts, keratinocytes, and macrophages across the concentrations tested. The peptide also downregulated inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and dampened NF-κB p65 phosphorylation, leaving the total NF-κB pool unchanged. As this exploratory study evaluated only low- and high-dose conditions, future studies incorporating intermediate doses will further refine the dose–response relationship and strengthen mechanistic understanding. Proteomic profiling revealed differential regulation of proteins associated with phosphorylation processes, redox homeostasis, and interferon-responsive pathways, including upregulation of Ppp1cc and downregulation of Lrpprc. Molecular docking suggested a potential interaction between TNFSNCTL and COX-2. These findings indicate that TNFSNCTL modulates oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling in macrophages, supporting its potential as a promising candidate for functional food or nutraceutical applications.

item.title: From Mitochondrial Targeting to Microbial Killing: Twinkle-Derived Peptides as an Emerging Class of Potent AMPs
item.description:
Abstract
Mitochondrial targeting sequences are short N-terminal peptides that direct proteins to mitochondria. Notably, their amphipathic α-helical architecture closely resembles that of many potent antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This structural convergence reflects the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria and suggests that contemporary mitochondrial targeting sequences may retain latent antimicrobial properties. Here, this evolutionary link was exploited to investigate the mitochondrial-targeting sequences of a Twinkle helicase as a scaffold for the rational design of a new class of antimicrobials. Using an in silico strategy, two peptides, TAMP1 (Twinkle AntiMicrobial Peptide1) and its optimized derivative, TAMP2 (Twinkle AntiMicrobial Peptide2), were designed starting from the mitochondrial targeting sequences of the Twinkle helicase from the Antarctic fish Notothenia coriiceps. Both 18-residue peptides were structurally and functionally characterized as proof of concept for mitochondrial targeting sequence-derived antimicrobials. They adopted stable amphipathic α-helical conformations and exhibited antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Notably, TAMP2 demonstrated enhanced efficacy, effectively targeting an extended panel of bacteria, including spoilage, foodborne, and multidrug-resistant pathogens, with MBC values in the range of 0.5–32 μM. Microscale thermophoresis and molecular dynamics simulations further supported these observations, indicating strong interactions with bacterial membrane mimetics and providing mechanistic insight into peptide activity. These findings establish Twinkle-derived mitochondrial targeting sequence peptides as a promising, scalable platform for developing a novel class of antimicrobial agents inspired by mitochondrial evolution.

item.title: Physicochemical Controls on Methane Adsorption Capacity of Coal Seams Beneath Red Beds: Roles of Pore Structure and Surface Chemistry
item.description:
Abstract
The abnormal occurrence of coalbed methane (CBM) beneath thick red beds poses a major challenge to gas disaster prevention and safe coal mining. Previous studies have mainly focused on the sealing capacity of red beds and their influence on CBM migration and accumulation, whereas the response of the underlying coal matrix, particularly its methane adsorption behavior, pore structure, and surface chemistry, remains insufficiently understood. Consequently, the mechanisms linking red beds occurrence conditions to variations in the methane storage capacity of underlying coal seams have not yet been fully quantified. Taking the Xutuan Coal Mine in the Huaibei Coalfield as a case study, this work integrates high-pressure methane adsorption–desorption tests, low-pressure N2/CO2 adsorption experiments, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy to reveal the effects of red beds on methane adsorption behavior, pore structure, and chemical composition of coal. The results show that, with increasing red beds thickness and decreasing distance between the coal seam and the red beds, micropore volume generally decreases, whereas the relative abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups increases. Correlation analysis further shows that methane adsorption capacity is positively correlated with micropore volume and negatively correlated with the relative abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups, with correlation coefficients of 1.0 and −1.0, respectively. These results indicate that both micropore structure and surface chemical characteristics are closely related to the variation in methane adsorption capacity. Combined with the geological characteristics of the red beds, the observed micropore variation may be related to stress-related pore compression, whereas the increase in oxygen-containing functional groups reflects changes in the surface chemical structure of the coal matrix. Fe-related oxidation is proposed as a geochemical hypothesis for the observed variation in oxygen-containing functional groups, based on the regional geological background of the red beds. Furthermore, a normalized red beds geometric influence index, k, was proposed to integrate red beds thickness and its spatial relationship with the coal seam. Field gas content exhibits a strong negative correlation with k, indicating that the proposed index can provide a quantitative reference for the relative evaluation of methane occurrence under comparable red beds geological conditions.

item.title: Multiphase W–V–Hf-Ta Mixed-Metal Oxides for Catalytic Oxidation of Toluene
item.description:
Abstract
Multiphase mixed-metal oxides (MMOs) containing W, V, Hf, Ta, and either Fe or Ti were synthesized by coprecipitation and evaluated as catalysts for toluene oxidation. Structural analysis determined the formation of multiphase crystalline systems, while energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy pointed out to homogeneous elemental distribution. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirmed that all elements are present in oxidized states, consistent with the formation of mixed-metal oxides. The catalytic activity of the prepared MMO was tested in a fixed-bed reactor in the toluene degradation process. A one-dimensional pseudohomogeneous model assuming first-order kinetics successfully described the experimental data. The Ti-containing catalyst showed slightly higher activity, achieving a lower toluene removal temperature and having a lower activation energy (139.27 kJ mol–1) in comparison to the Fe-containing catalyst (145.41 kJ mol–1). The obtained results demonstrate that the investigated multiphase MMOs are promising candidates for volatile organic compounds removal.

item.title: Tools for Prediction of Alkyne p K a Values: Calculation of Hydrogen Exchange Barriers and NMR Chemical Shifts
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate prediction of acidity in terminal alkynes is critical for understanding their chemical behavior in isotope labeling, synthesis design, and drug development. In this study, we evaluate multiple quantum-chemical strategies to identify a reliable and simple computational approach for estimating alkyne acidities. A range of descriptors, including thermodynamic proton and hydrogen atom transfers, reaction energy profiles, vibrational and magnetic properties, and atomic charge distributions, were assessed across a representative set of alkynes. Only two approaches demonstrated predictive performance aligned with experimental data. The first involves calculation of energy barriers for hydrogen exchange, which shows a linear correlation with known pKa values and offers applicability across alkyl-, aryl-, and fluoro-substituted alkynes. The second leverages computed acetylenic proton chemical shifts, which provide valid predictions for a limited subset of alkynes. In contrast, descriptors such as IR frequencies, 13C NMR shifts, and atomic charges failed to yield accurate estimates. We extended our predictions to pharmaceuticals with terminal alkyne groups─such as ethynylestradiol, deprenyl, and 5-ethynyluracil─for which experimental acidity data are currently unavailable. The proposed workflow combines computational efficiency with mechanistic relevance and may serve as a practical tool for chemists seeking to assess the acid–base properties of terminal alkynes in silico.

item.title: Al 3+ -Modified Melamine Sponge for Downhole Oil–Water Separation
item.description:
Abstract
Increasing water production during the later stages of oilfield development generates large volumes of produced water with low oil content, creating challenges for efficient treatment. Downhole oil–water separation can reduce the treatment load of surface facilities but requires materials with high oil selectivity and stable performance. Herein, a hydrophobically modified melamine sponge was prepared through a simple AlCl3 immersion method. SEM-EDS, FTIR, and XPS confirmed the introduction of Al3+ onto the sponge surface and supported its interaction with electron-donating sites in the melamine framework, while the original porous structure was preserved. The modified sponge exhibited water contact angles above 130° and adsorption capacities of approximately 100 g/g for crude oil and 89 g/g for paraffin oil. TGA indicated a modest improvement in thermal stability. Oil–water separation was further evaluated through adsorption, in situ extraction, and filtration. The adsorption mode achieved nearly 100% separation efficiency, while in situ extraction reached 97.5% efficiency at a rate of 6.25 mL/s. Filtration further demonstrated the potential for polishing low-oil-content wastewater. These results highlight Al3+-modified melamine sponge as a simple and versatile material for staged oil–water separation in oilfield applications.

item.title: Simulation of the Deformation Process of a Freely Rising Bubble Using the Lattice Boltzmann Method
item.description:
Abstract
Bubbles exhibit nonlinear motion characteristics in liquids, with their interfaces undergoing significant deformation during movement, resulting in complex and diverse situations. In this paper, the lattice Boltzmann method is employed to numerically simulate the deformation behavior of a freely rising single bubble. The focus is on examining the effects of bubble size, surface tension, liquid viscosity, and liquid density on bubble deformation and obtaining the variation of the Weber number of bubble deformation. The results indicate that the essence of bubble deformation lies in the dynamic interplay between inertial forces, viscous forces, and surface tension. The Weber number serves as an effective comprehensive indicator of the relative importance of these three factors. Notably, surface tension emerges as the pivotal factor inhibiting deformation, whereas liquid density and bubble size facilitate deformation by amplifying inertial forces. The role of liquid viscosity exhibits nonmonotonicity, stemming from its dual function as both a damping dissipator and a shear deformation transmitter.

item.title: A Composable 3D-Printed Platform for Rapid Sequential Sample Injection in Mass Spectrometry
item.description:
Abstract
We developed a composable 3D-printed platform for rapid sequential sample injection in mass spectrometry (MS). The platform works in a well plate-like format and allows direct loading of discrete sample droplets by micropipette or automated liquid handling. Droplets are separated by air gaps during transport and are directly coupled to MS through capillary vibrating sharp-edge spray ionization (cVSSI). Liquid-infused surface treatment was used to improve compatibility of the 3D-printed microchannels with MS analysis. The platform was evaluated for device operation, throughput, quantitative performance, and carryover. A throughput of ∼20 s per sample was achieved at 50 μL/min. Quantitative analysis of lysine gave a linear response with R2 = 0.9986, and carryover was evaluated across chemically distinct small molecules. These results demonstrate that the platform supports air-separated droplet transport, rapid sequential analysis of different samples, and quantitative MS measurements in a simple, modular, and customizable format.

item.title: Signal-Analytics Modeling of Fluorescence Maximum Time-to-Detection (TTD + ) for E. coli in Treated Wastewater: A Joint Censoring and Sensor Model Approach Part II
item.description:
Abstract
Water security is a global priority and relies on reliable microbiological monitoring in treated effluents. In this work, we investigate a sensor-analytics component of Escherichia coli (E. coli) monitoring in treated wastewater through fluorescence time courses acquired with a miniaturized, Internet of Things-enabled incubation platform, named the Optical Bacterial Growth Sensor–Fluorescence Detector. The signal arises from hydrolysis of a β-d-glucuronide substrate mediated by E. coli-expressed β-glucuronidase activity, yielding characteristic kinetic profiles over time. Our primary target is the extraction and probabilistic modeling of the upper time-to-detection, TTD+, an operational timing feature of the recorded fluorescence response. In practical terms, TTD+ retrospectively identifies the onset of the upper stable signal region under the adopted criterion, providing a timing summary for assay duration planning. To model this time-domain boundary, we adopt the Joint Censoring and Sensor Model Approach (JCSMA) and further extend it by deriving analytical expressions for ordinary moments and entropy measures, including Rényi and Shannon entropies. The empirical comparison favors JCSMA within the evaluated model set, while simulation characterizes the sampling behavior of selected statistics under the fitted model. The resulting probabilities and quantiles provide summaries for assay duration planning under the adopted conditions. The study does not evaluate analytical figures of merit for E. coli quantification or the association between TTD+ and reference most probable number values.

item.title: Wettability-Controlled Hydrophobic Deep Eutectic Solvents for Sustainable and Rapid Removal of Hexavalent Chromium
item.description:
Abstract
The removal of hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) from industrial effluents remains challenging for conventional solvent extraction systems due to sluggish mass transfer, limited extraction capacity, and the inherent toxicity of volatile organic compounds. Here, we report a wettability-modulated strategy to overcome these limitations using hydrophobic deep eutectic solvents (HDESs) based on quaternary ammonium salts and fatty acids. By correlating the contact angle, viscosity, and hydrogen-bonding network with extraction performance, we identify the optimized HDES, [N8881][Br]-OA(1:2), which exhibits a remarkably low viscosity (147.6 cP at 298.2 K) and a favorable contact angle (34.4°), enabling rapid interfacial anion exchange. This extractant achieves a single-stage Cr(VI) recovery exceeding 99% within only 10 min at an initial concentration of 500 mg·L–1 under an oil-to-water ratio of 1:50. Mechanistic investigations confirm a reversible Br–/HCrO4– anion-exchange pathway, while thermodynamic analysis reveals an endothermic and entropy-driven process. Notably, the HDES maintains over 95% extraction efficiency after 12 successive regeneration cycles without structural degradation and outperforms the benchmark solvent methyl isobutyl ketone (MIBK) by a factor of 12. This work demonstrates that tailoring the wettability of HDESs provides a green, sustainable, and industrially viable platform for the ultrafast decontamination of Cr(VI)-laden wastewater, with significant potential for scalable water treatment applications.

item.title: An Experimental Study on the Quantitative Mesoscopic Roughness Characteristics of Rock Using the Size Reduction Method
item.description:
Abstract
The development of emerging clean energy technologies, including CO2 geological sequestration, enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), and underground hydrogen storage, faces a critical scientific and engineering challenge: the accurate characterization of complex fracture morphology in subsurface rock formations. Accurate quantification of fracture morphology is a fundamental prerequisite for engineering design and numerical simulation. However, current methodologies for fracture characterization often fail to effectively distinguish between detailed features such as fracture orientation and surface roughness, leading to imprecise characterization results that directly impact the quality of engineering implementation. This study introduces an innovative theoretical framework─the size reduction method─which isolates detailed roughness from surface tortuosity. Additionally, a novel detailed roughness index, Ra-r, is proposed to complement this method. Utilizing this advanced approach, the research conducts a comprehensive comparison of surface roughness across various fracture types: different regions within a single fracture, natural versus hydraulic fractures within the same specimen, fractures of identical lithology, and fractures of differing lithologies. The findings reveal several critical insights: First, within a single fracture, the roughness at turning positions is significantly lower than that in positions with a unidirectional trend, approximately 31.9% of the latter. Second, hydraulic fractures in carbonatite specimens exhibit higher roughness compared to natural fractures. Third, the presence of quartz mineral fillings reduces the roughness of carbonatite hydraulic fractures to 69.4%. Lastly, a comparison between carbonatite and shale fractures indicates that the roughness of shale hydraulic fractures is about 50.6% of that of carbonatite, while the roughness of natural fractures in shale is approximately 51.4% of that of carbonatite. This research offers significant contributions to the theoretical understanding and practical applications of fracture flow dynamics, providing a robust foundation for future studies and industrial implementations in the field of resource extraction.

item.title: Thermodynamically Constrained Deep Learning for Hydrogen Sorption Prediction: Overcoming Classical Isotherm Generalization Failure through Physics-Informed Cross-Lithology Transferability
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate prediction of hydrogen sorption in fine-grained geological materials is essential for subsurface energy systems. While classical isotherm models describe individual samples effectively, they fail to generalize across heterogeneous populations, with R2 dropping from 0.80–0.90 for single-sample fits to 0.09–0.38 for aggregated data sets. This limitation demonstrates that predictive models must explicitly account for intrinsic material properties and fundamental physical constraints. We present a thermodynamics-informed, physics-regularized neural network framework designed to improve predictive accuracy and cross-lithology generalization. The framework integrates three core components: a seven-category physics-informed feature engineering scheme generating 62 thermodynamically meaningful descriptors, a multiterm loss function enforcing saturation limits and monotonic pressure responses through penalty-weighted terms, and an architecture-diverse ten-member ensemble with post hoc temperature-scaling calibration to provide reliable uncertainty estimates. Van’t Hoff temperature dependence is incorporated through thermodynamic feature engineering, with all model components integrated within a three-phase curriculum training strategy that progressively introduces physical regularization. On a random-split holdout set, the framework achieves R2 = 0.9544, RMSE = 0.0484 mmol/g, and MAE = 0.0231 mmol/g, with a 98.6% monotonicity satisfaction rate and zero nonphysical negative predictions. Because random splits primarily evaluate interpolation within the observed distribution, we prioritize leave-one-lithology-out (LOLO) validation to assess physical generalization under distribution shift. When entire geological classes are withheld from training, the framework retains R2 = 0.723 for coal and 0.794 for shale, outperforming a well-tuned random forest baseline (R2 = 0.631 and 0.712, respectively) by 14.6% and 11.5%, respectively. These results support the effectiveness of thermodynamic constraints as a generalization scaffold across geological boundaries, providing a practical foundation for evaluating formations whose lithological classes are absent from the training data.

item.title: Comparative HPHC Emission Profiles of Combustible and Alternative Nicotine Products in South Africa: Development of a Relative HPHC Emission Index
item.description:
Abstract
Alternative nicotine and tobacco products are increasingly available in South Africa, yet independent comparative data on their harmful and potentially harmful constituent (HPHC) emission profiles remain limited. The aim of this study was to compare mainstream emissions from an illicit combustible cigarette (Brand X), IQOS ILUMA heated tobacco products (TEREA Amber and TEREA Turquoise), a VEEV Now Ultra Mint disposable electronic nicotine delivery system, and ZYN modern oral nicotine pouches, with the 1R6F reference cigarette included as a combustible benchmark. Combustion-related markers CO, NO and NOx were evaluated in TEREA aerosols under synthetic-air and nitrogen atmospheres, while nine WHO-priority HPHCs were quantified using standardized analytical methods. Emissions were normalized to 100 cm3 of nominal puff volume where applicable. Brand X produced high emissions across the measured HPHC panel, including 4.91 ± 0.28 mg/100 cm3 CO, 248.67 ± 14.55 μg/100 cm3 acetaldehyde, 23.66 ± 2.27 μg/100 cm3 acrolein, 11.33 ± 1.43 μg/100 cm3 formaldehyde, 17.20 ± 0.75 μg/100 cm3 1,3-butadiene and 13.29 ± 1.01 μg/100 cm3 benzene. TEREA aerosols generated CO, NO and NOx concentrations below the BSI PAS 8850:2020 combustion-marker thresholds under both atmospheres, supporting the absence of combustion under the tested conditions. Across the WHO-9 panel, TEREA aerosols showed substantially lower emissions than combustible cigarette smoke, while VEEV showed quantifiable acetaldehyde and formaldehyde at low levels and most other target constituents below detection limits. Nicotine pouches showed a similarly restricted profile. Among TEREA variants, only NNN remained different after Holm adjustment. To integrate the multidimensional HPHC data, a Relative HPHC Emission Index (RHEI) was developed by normalizing each constituent to the highest emission among VEEV, TEREA Turquoise and Brand X and combining the nine constituent scores using equal weighting. The RHEI showed clear separation among the three products, with Brand X having the highest relative HPHC emission profile, TEREA Turquoise an intermediate profile, and VEEV the lowest. These findings provide an analytical basis for product-specific evaluation and surveillance of nicotine products in South Africa.

item.title: Effect of In Mole Fraction on Gamma Ray Shielding Properties of In x Al 1–x As Material
item.description:
Abstract
The gamma-ray shielding performance of InxAl1–xAs with different In mole fractions was systematically investigated via the Phy-X/PSD. Key shielding parameters including mass attenuation coefficient (MAC), linear attenuation coefficient (LAC), half-value layer (HVL), tenth-value layer (TVL), mean free path (MFP), atomic cross-section (ACS), electronic cross-section (ECS), effective atomic number (Zeff), effective electron density (Neff), effective conductivity (Ceff), R-value, and equivalent atomic number (Zeq) were calculated over the energy range of 0.015–15 MeV. The results demonstrate that the MAC, LAC, ACS, ECS, Zeff, Ceff, and Zeq values increase with a rising In mole fraction, with In0.8Al0.2As exhibiting the highest values among the studied samples, alongside lower HVL, TVL, and MFP values. At equivalent photon energies, a linear correlation was observed between HVL, TVL, and MFP and the In mole fraction as x increased from 0.25 to 0.8. To quantify the composition-driven enhancement, a comprehensive shielding performance index (ICSP) was defined, and In0.8Al0.2As showed up to a 369% improvement at 0.1 MeV relative to In0.25Al0.75As.These findings suggest that increasing In content effectively enhances the gamma-ray attenuation capability of InAlAs materials. Furthermore, the observed linear relationships between shielding parameters and composition enable the prediction and optimization of shielding performance through compositional tuning, providing a theoretical foundation for the compositional design of III–V compound semiconductors in radiation shielding applications.

item.title: Energy-Efficient and Low-Temperature Gaseous Concentration Swing Adsorption (GCSA)-Based Regeneration Method Utilizing Hydrogen Sweep for Direct Air Capture
item.description:
Abstract
Solid sorbent-based direct air capture (DAC) is a promising pathway for durable carbon dioxide removal (CDR), but large-scale deployment remains constrained by sorbent degradation and the high cost and energy associated with temperature-vacuum swing adsorption (TVSA). Here, we introduce a hydrogen (H2)-enabled gaseous concentration swing adsorption (GCSA) process that eliminates vacuum and enables regeneration at 35–70 °C using a closed-loop H2 sweep with a commercial amine sorbent. By lowering the CO2 partial pressure under reducing conditions near ambient pressure, H2-GCSA achieves effective regeneration with reduced thermal severity and suppressed oxidative degradation. Accelerated testing between 65 and 95 °C under oxidative and anaerobic environments demonstrates superior sorbent stability over 100 h under oxygen-free conditions. A process-integrated techno-economic analysis for a 100,000 tCO2/yr modular DAC plant, utilizing a total of less than 8.5 tons of H2 and incorporating downstream H2/CO2 separation via pressure swing adsorption (PSA), projects an energy demand of 2.78 GJ/tCO2 (775 KWh/tCO2) and a capture cost of 81 USD/tCO2, representing a 2–3× lower capital cost and 1.5–4× lower energy demand relative to TVSA. Further process integration using low-grade waste heat and PSA elimination reduces the energy demand to 0.85 GJ/tCO2 (235 KWh/tCO2), with projected costs approaching 31 USD/tCO2. Sensitivity analysis indicates that the sorbent cost below 95 USD/kg enables DAC below 100 USD/tCO2. Collectively, these results demonstrate that H2 sweep-mediated GCSA offers a scalable, lower-energy alternative to vacuum-driven (TVSA) regeneration on a wide range of sorbents, eliminating the sorbent material development risks and addressing a central bottleneck in solid-sorbent DAC.

item.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization of Surfactin Titer Produced by Bacillus subtilis MTCC 2423 from Minimum Fermentation Data with Experimental Validation
item.description:
Abstract
Optimizing surfactin production from a wild-type Bacillus sp., is challenging due to complex microbial growth kinetics, nonlinear interactions among process variables, and the lack of mechanistic models to describe surfactin production. Therefore, the present study develops data-driven machine learning models to optimize surfactin production from Bacillus subtilis MTCC 2423 under limited fermentation data. First, 25 batch fermentation experiments were performed to obtain surfactin titers under varied conditions of temperature, agitation speed, and inoculum volume, generated using a central composite design (CCD) integrated with maximin Latin hypercube sampling (LHS). Subsequently, machine learning models, viz, multivariable least-squares regression (MVLSR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), support vector regression (SVR), and random forest (RF), were trained and evaluated using the nested leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) to achieve robust prediction of the surfactin titer. Hyperparameter tuning of the models was performed using a genetic algorithm (GA) and grid search. Both the GPR and SVR outperformed the other models and demonstrated comparable predictive performance on the unseen data, producing the LOOCV R2 of 0.89 and 0.86, and LOOCV RMSE of 0.6 and 0.67, respectively. Subsequently, the mean response surface plots were constructed using the GPR model to illustrate the effects of nonlinear interactions among the input features on the surfactin titer. Finally, a GPR-based constrained optimization yielded an optimal surfactin titer of 5.72 g L–1, compared to the base-case value of 1.49 g L–1, while identifying the optimal process variables. The data-driven optimization results closely agreed with the experimentally validated surfactin titer of 5.75 ± 0.09 g L–1, demonstrating high model reliability and predictive accuracy. Our experimental design approach, integrated with machine-learning-driven optimization using limited experimental data, can be adopted across various bioprocess sectors to achieve substantial improvements in surfactin titer.

item.title: Characterization of Extracellular Vesicles from Attenuated and Virulent Leishmania amazonensis Promastigotes Reveals Distinct Proteomic Signatures
item.description:
Abstract
Leishmaniasis is a group of endemic diseases caused by different species of Leishmania. Virulence factors produced by Leishmania can be found in extracellular vesicles (EVs), a heterogeneous group of particles released by cells that are involved in cell-to-cell communication. Herein, we demonstrated that Leishmania amazonensis subjected to three in vivo passages exhibited exacerbated virulence, while prolonged culture resulted in an attenuated profile. The morphological characterization of EVs released by these parasites showed no significant differences. However, proteomic analysis revealed enrichment of proteins associated with proteolysis in EVs released by virulent parasites. In addition, these EVs showed significantly higher proteasome activity compared to EVs from attenuated L. amazonensis promastigotes. Attenuated and virulent parasites incorporated EVs. However, we observed a significant increase in murine macrophage infectivity by virulent parasites following uptake of autologous EVs. Thus, our findings show that L. amazonensis parasites with distinct virulence profiles release EVs with differences in the relative abundance of their protein cargo, which may contribute to the maintenance or enhancement of parasite infectivity.

item.title: Vapor Phase Infiltration of Metal Oxides for Water Treatment Membranes: Potential and Limitations
item.description:
Abstract
Membrane-based water treatment processes are critical for global water security, yet current state-of-the-art polymeric membranes face limitations in mechanical, chemical, and thermal stability. Ceramic membranes, on the other hand, foul less, are easy to clean, and have high modulus values, but they are brittle and less permeable when used as dense membranes. Vapor phase infiltration (VPI) of metal oxides, a derivative of atomic layer deposition (ALD) that transforms organic polymers into organic–inorganic hybrid materials, offers a novel method to modify polymeric membranes and allow them to have the advantages of both polymeric and ceramic membranes. In this review, we combine insights from the use of VPI with polymeric substrates and organic solvent separation membranes to provide our view of the potential and limitations of VPI for enhancing water treatment membranes. We examine how VPI of metal oxides improves the mechanical strength, which is relevant to compaction-resistant reverse osmosis supports, and chemical stability, which could play a role in membrane chlorine and extreme-pH tolerance. We also critically evaluate the associated trade-offs, most notably potential reductions in water permeance arising from the intrinsically lower water permeability of metal oxides. We further identify ion exchange membranes and electrodialysis as especially promising targets, where suppressed water transport is advantageous for ion–ion selectivity. Together, these insights clarify where VPI of metal oxides can most effectively advance emerging membrane-based water treatment technologies.

item.title: Performance Evaluation of CO 2 Huff-n-Puff in Shale Oil Reservoirs: Multiwell Huff-n-Puff and Parameter Optimization
item.description:
Abstract
CO2 huff-n-puff (HnP) is an established enhanced oil recovery (EOR) method for shale oil reservoirs. However, its field-scale implementation in multiwell fractured systems remains challenging because fracture-controlled interwell connectivity can cause operational interference and inefficient CO2 allocation. A field-scale numerical model of the HH shale oil reservoir, incorporating complex natural and hydraulic fracture networks, was constructed and history-matched against field production data, followed by a structured sequential one-factor-at-a-time analysis and descriptive Spearman rank-correlation screening of the associations between operational parameters and performance indicators. Results indicate that, for the calibrated HH reservoir realization, the intragroup synchronized and intergroup asynchronous strategy achieved the highest cumulative incremental oil production among the investigated strategies (9.59 × 104 t), together with a CO2 utilization efficiency of 0.266 t oil/t CO2. This performance was associated with the cross-group pressure contrast observed under the asynchronous operation of the two well groups. Rank-correlation screening indicated that cycle number and cyclic CO2 injection mass showed the strongest associations with oil recovery and CO2 utilization efficiency, respectively, within the investigated cases. Within the investigated ranges and under the experimentally constrained diffusion setting of the calibrated HH reservoir model, 45 days and 450 t/d were identified as the preferred soaking time and injection rate, respectively. Extending the soaking time from 45 to 55 days yielded only marginal improvements, whereas increasing the injection rate from 450 to 600 t/d slightly reduced both incremental oil production and CO2 utilization efficiency. Furthermore, compared with the uniform injection scheme, the differentiated injection scheme maintained a comparable OOIP-based recovery factor (15.97% versus 15.84%) while reducing the cumulative gross CO2 injection mass from 36.0 × 104 to 33.1 × 104 t, corresponding to an 8.1% reduction. The EOR-oriented CO2 utilization efficiency consequently increased from 0.274 to 0.305 t oil/t CO2. Therefore, its principal benefit was the more efficient use of the injected CO2 rather than a substantial increase in ultimate oil recovery. This work provides a field-scale numerical workflow for designing and evaluating coordinated multiwell CO2 HnP operations in fractured shale oil reservoirs.

item.title: Data Characterization and Multi-Plant Data Integration Strategies for Artificial Neural Network Modeling in Palm Oil Refining
item.description:
Abstract
Real-time quality monitoring in palm oil refining is often hindered by laboratory delays, which can be mitigated through the development of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) soft sensors. However, the effectiveness of these models is constrained by the characteristics of available process data. To address this, this study establishes a quantitative framework for assessing data set suitability by analyzing industrial data from three refineries using coefficient of variation (CV) statistics and self-organizing map (SOM) visualizations, with a feedforward neural network (FFN) used as a baseline model. Results show that process variables with CV exceeding 50% consistently yield better FFN performance than those below 50%. An integration strategy between different refineries was introduced to overcome the limitation of single-plant data and improve model performance to above 80% prediction accuracy for FFA content and Red Lovibond color. To test whether this improvement resulted from model capacity rather than data variability. The results further showed that data variability significantly affects model performance rather than model architecture. These findings establish CV as a practical criterion for data set suitability in ANN modeling for palm oil refining, offering an approach other chemical process industries facing similarly low-variation data may adapt.

item.title: Covalent Surface Modification of Polyester Fabric with Carvacrol and Eugenol
item.description:
Abstract
Synthetic fibers such as polyester (PES) are highly valued for their strength and low cost, yet their inherent hydrophobicity and poor dyeability remain significant challenges. To address these limitations sustainably, this study presents a novel surface modification of PES that combines mild lipase-catalyzed hydrolysis to generate reactive surface carboxyl groups, followed by direct esterification with the natural phenolic compounds carvacrol and eugenol. The efficacy of this functionalization was evaluated using FTIR, UV–vis, contact angle, SEM, and thermal analysis. Optimization revealed that a 40 wt % oil concentration provided the optimal balance, achieving effective surface incorporation of 8.3 mmol g–1 of fabric for carvacrol and 6.1 mmol g–1 for eugenol. FTIR, along with 5-cycle wash-fastness tests, indicated the durable formation of covalent ester bonds. The resulting modified fabrics exhibited excellent hydrophilicity (contact angle reduced from 116.17° to 0° with immediate absorption) and significantly enhanced dye diffusion and color fastness matching untreated standards. Additionally, incorporating these terpenes imparted high-value properties, notably reducing flame propagation (remaining length increasing from 2.7 cm to 4.1–4.3 cm) and inhibiting Candida albicans proliferation by 48–90%. These findings highlight a promising, eco-friendly pathway for the durable, covalent functionalization of polyester textiles.

item.title: Laser-Induced Graphene Modified with Gold Nanoparticles for Dengue Biomarker Detection: Toward Portable and Flexible Biosensing Platforms for Early Diagnosis
item.description:
Abstract
Dengue remains a major public health challenge in tropical and subtropical regions, where early detection can support timely clinical management. Nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), released during the acute phase of infection, is an important biomarker for early dengue detection. Here, we report a flexible electrochemical immunosensor based on laser-induced graphene (LIG), a hierarchically porous three-dimensional carbon material produced by laser irradiation of polyimide and functionalized with gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) through a simple electroless deposition process. The incorporation of AuNPs reduced the impedance of the LIG electrode, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and increased the electrochemically accessible surface area. Structural, morphological, electrochemical, and surface wettability characterizations confirmed the successive modification steps of the sensing platform. The resulting biosensor exhibited a logarithmic response to DENV-2 NS1 over the experimentally evaluated concentration range of 10–1000 ng/mL, with a calculated limit of detection of 3.3 ng/mL. The sensor showed reproducible responses and low cross-reactivity toward Zika virus NS1 under the investigated conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining porous LIG and AuNPs for electrochemical NS1 detection and provide a basis for the further development of flexible electrochemical biosensors for dengue NS1 detection.

item.title: Enhanced Electrical Output for Triboelectric Nanogenerator Based on Cobalt-Doped Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework as a Multifunctional Filler for Negative Tribolayer
item.description:
Abstract
Developing more efficient triboelectric nanogenerators raises several questions about how to tune the dielectric constant, porosity, and charge-trapping ability of friction layers. Herein, the modification of the standard Ecoflex layer was achieved by the incorporation of pure imidazolate zeolitic frameworks (ZIF-8 and ZIF-67) and modified structures (Cox%/ZIF-8), as a strategy for tuning the dielectric constant of the heterostructure (ZIF/Ecoflex) and the charge transfer rate by progressive incorporation of a cobalt-doping element. As a result, the dielectric constant varied from (2.81 ± 0.28) for pure Ecoflex to (3.29 ± 0.01) for the ZIF-67/Ecoflex composite, while fixed-point Kelvin probe experiments indicate faster charge rearrangement in ZIF-67-based composites. As a consequence of the direct relationship between the transferred charge density and the variation in the dielectric constant of the friction layer, the modification provided by the ZIF incorporation into Ecoflex resulted in an improvement of 58% in the short-circuit current and 170% in the open-circuit voltage measured at 4 Hz, characterizing important findings for cobalt-doping effects in ZIF derivatives applied as a nanofiller in the friction layer for TENGs.

item.title: Gas-Phase Reactivity of AuSiO 3 – Anion Clusters with n-Alkanes (C 1 –C 4 ): Distinguishing Capture, Stabilized Association, and C–H Bond Activation
item.description:
Abstract
The reactivity of heteronuclear gold-silicon oxide cluster anion AuSiO3– toward small alkanes (C1–C4) has been experimentally investigated at room temperature by employing a homemade reflectron time-of-flight mass spectrometer. Experimental results reveal distinct reaction channels for these systems, which produce hydrogen-containing dissociation products (SiO3H–) and associative adducts (AuSiO3CnH2n+2–, n = 1–4). While the total depletion (capture) rate increases with increasing chain length, the branching ratio of dissociation products correspondingly decreases. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the two-fold-coordinated gold ion (Au+) anchored on the AuSiO3– cluster proceeds via an oxidative addition mechanism involving homolytic bond cleavage. Both RRKM calculations and MESMER master-equation simulations reveal that for larger alkanes such as C4H10, the rapidly growing density of vibrational states with increasing chain length shifts the competition from product dissociation toward collisional stabilization, thereby favoring associative adduct formation over dissociation pathways─a stark contrast to the behavior observed in the AuSiO3––CH4 reaction. This work provides novel insights into the competition among collisional capture, stabilized association, and C–H bond activation in small-molecule alkanes.

item.title: Large-Area Metasurfaces for Enhanced Fluorescence Imaging
item.description:
Abstract
All-dielectric metasurfaces have been extensively applied to three-dimensional displays, vortex beam generation, beam steering, and luminescence enhancement. However, studies on all-dielectric metasurfaces for enhancing biofluorescence imaging remain relatively scarce. In this study, an anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) template is employed to fabricate a large-area silicon metasurface embedded in PDMS to serve as a fluorescence imaging slide. Under the excitation of the electromagnetic dipole resonance of metasurface, the cells stained with iFluor 555-phalloidin on the metasurface film exhibit a fluorescence enhancement potentially arising from the combined contributions of Purcell-related radiative decay-rate modification, local excitation-field enhancement, and changes in fluorescence collection efficiency, substantially improving the fluorescence imaging quality. The experimental results demonstrate that when the silicon metasurface embedded in PDMS serves as a fluorescence imaging slide, the fluorescence imaging intensity is enhanced by a factor of approximately 3.38. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of large-area all-dielectric metasurfaces fabricated via the AAO template method for enhanced fluorescence imaging. This finding broadens the scope of all-dielectric metasurfaces with large area for biomedical fluorescence imaging.

item.title: Charge-Induced Conductance Modulation and Capacitive Properties of Two-Layer–like 2γ-In 2 Se 3 : Insights from Density Functional Theory
item.description:
Abstract
We investigate the field- and charge-driven electronic instabilities in two-layer–like 2γ-In2Se3 with implications for charge-induced conductance modulation. Using density functional theory, we examine the effects of an external electric field and charge doping on the electronic structure. While the electric field primarily redistributes charge carriers, charge doping directly controls the occupation of the Mexican-hat–like states and the associated van Hove singularity near the valence-band edge. The charge-controlled occupation of the Mexican-hat-like states governs both spin polarization and in-plane conductivity, thereby providing a microscopic mechanism for conductance modulation. This work suggests that two-layer-like 2γ-In2Se3 may provide a useful platform for exploring field- and charge-tunable electronic responses relevant to nanoelectronics.

item.title: Extraction of Calcium from Steel Slag via Low-Temperature Chlorination Roasting and Water Leaching for the Preparation of CaCO 3
item.description:
Abstract
This paper proposes a novel coupled process of “low-temperature chlorination roasting with NH4Cl─water leaching for calcium separation─carbonation precipitation” to achieve selective recovery and utilization of calcium from steel slag. Thermodynamic calculations indicate the presence of two reaction pathways in the system: solid–solid chlorination and gas–solid chlorination mediated by HCl. Among these, the gas-phase chlorination reaction exhibits a stronger thermodynamic spontaneity. Phase analysis of the raw steel slag shows that calcium is primarily found in the phases of Ca2SiO4, Ca2Fe2O5, and Al14Ca12O33, with a positive correlation to the contents of silicon, iron, and aluminum. The roasting temperature and holding time have been identified as the core factors affecting the calcium chlorination rate. Under optimal conditions (temperature of 300 °C, holding time of 40 min, mass ratio of NH4Cl to steel slag of 2:1, and steel slag particle size of 75–106 μm), the calcium chlorination rate can reach 92.47%. Kinetic analysis based on the unreacted core shrinking model confirms that this chlorination process is controlled by the diffusion of the solid product layer. The resulting calcium-containing leachate, after carbonation precipitation, yields well-formed, uniformly shaped rhombohedral calcite particles.

item.title: Ultrasmall Superparamagnetic Fe 3 O 4 Nanoparticles Green-Synthesized with Cosmos caudatus : Phytochemical Surface Coordination and Suppression of MCF-7 Migration
item.description:
Abstract
Phytochemical-mediated synthesis of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPION) is dominated by a narrow set of plant substrates, and extending this chemical space to phylogenetically distinct species remains an open question. Herein, we report the first application of Cosmos caudatus Kunth leaf extract, rich in quercetin glycosides, catechins, and chlorogenic acid, to the green sonochemical synthesis of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (CC-SPION), benchmarked against an extract-free control (Bare-SPION). Acoustic cavitation combined with phytochemical reduction produced a crystalline inverse-spinel iron oxide in 25 min at near ambient temperature. TEM revealed near-monodisperse, semispherical primary particles of 7.30 ± 0.88 nm smaller than green-synthesized iron oxides in related studies; the TEM primary-particle diameter (7.30 nm) and XRD crystallite size (7.25 nm) were in close agreement, with FE-SEM reporting larger drying-induced aggregates (7.7–17.5 nm). Multipeak XRD analysis showed the crystallite size fell from 11.61 nm (Bare-SPION) to 7.25 nm (CC-SPION). Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) corroborated the elemental compositions, whereas Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) substantiated the existence of Cosmos caudatus chemicals within the nanoparticle composition. This coordinated phytochemical corona raised the zeta-potential magnitude from −20.4 to −42.5 mV, conferring electrosteric stabilization (PDI ≈ 0.08). VSM confirmed superparamagnetism at 298 K (Ms = 43.99 emu/g; with no coercivity and remanence). CC-SPION was noncytotoxic to HEK-293 and MCF-7 cells across 31.25–500 μg Fe/mL (ISO 10993–5; viability ≥70%), reduced MCF-7 wound closure over 24–48 h, and showed dose-dependent cell association/localization. These findings establish C. caudatus sonochemistry as a route to mechanistically well-defined ultrasmall biocompatible SPION for prospective MRI and antimigratory applications.

item.title: Solution-Processed Ge 25 S 75 and Ge 25 Se 75 Thin Films─Influence of the Solution Preparation Pathway
item.description:
Abstract
Solution processing of chalcogenide thin films is an attractive alternative to vacuum-based deposition due to its low cost and scalability. We demonstrate a novel approach for preparing chalcogen-rich Ge–S and Ge–Se chalcogenide thin films from Ge33S67 and Ge33Se67 source bulk glasses by dissolving elemental chalcogen in the source bulk glass solution. This method allows for the preparation of chalcogen-rich thin films with a composition different from that of the source bulk glass. Two routes for chalcogen addition (the co-dissolution of bulk glass with chalcogen and the addition of chalcogen into a previously prepared bulk glass solution) were tested to study potential changes in dissolution chemistry and thus thin-film optical properties. The prepared solutions and deposited thin films were compared with the solutions and films produced by dissolving bulk glass of the targeted composition. Regardless of the preparation route, the solutions exhibited similar dissolution product structures, and the thin films possessed comparable composition, structure, and optical properties within the resolution and reproducibility of the applied methods, demonstrating the viability of both methods for the preparation of chalcogenide thin films. The presented method provides a new, simpler route for thin-film preparation.

item.title: Platform Synthesis for the Rapid Construction of V-Shaped and Cruciform Push–Pull Compounds
item.description:
Abstract
We report the modular synthesis of cruciform push–pull compounds from V-shaped di- and trisubstituted thiophenes obtained from commercially available 2,3-dibromothiophene (DBT) via sequential couplings using the concept of “platform synthesis”. Orthogonal C2/C3 functionalization with EDOT-and naphthothiophene-based molecular modules yielded a library of 8 V-shaped, sterically hindered π-conjugated derivatives. Coupling in C5 with electron-deficient benzothiadiazole units, to complete the “platform” synthetic sequence, afforded two different “cruciform-like” push–pull luminophores emitting in the deep red region of the visible spectrum. Photophysical and electrochemical studies, supported by calculations, revealed that the substitution pattern on DBT is crucial in tuning both emission efficiency and the bathochromic shifts, inducing aggregation-induced enhanced emission (AIEE) in one derivative. This work highlights the versatility of platform synthesis in the realization of relevant materials for optoelectronic applications.

item.title: Alkyl Imidazolium Cation-Supported Poly(terphenyl- co -fluorene isatin) Anion Exchange Membrane for Anion Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
item.description:
Abstract
Anion exchange membrane (AEM) is the core component of alkaline fuel cells. Current research still faces bottlenecks such as the difficulty in synergizing ion conductivity and alkali stability, and the inhibition of reaction kinetics by adsorption of ionomer catalysts. In this work, a new ether-free poly(terphenyl-co-fluorene isatin) polymer backbone was developed. Alkyl imidazole with a unique π-conjugated delocalized structure was selected as a cation to develop a series of imidazole cation-loaded comb-shaped poly(terphenyl-co-fluorene isatin) polyelectrolytes (PTFI-IZ-n). The additional hydrophobic structure on the imidazole cation provides a driving force for the self-assembly of ion clusters. PTFI-IZ-8 AEM exhibits the most developed phase separation morphology and exhibits a high OH– conductivity of 140.61 mS/cm at 80 °C. The long comb-like alkyl chain in PTFI-IZ-8 AEM effectively protects the stability of the cation. After 1200 h in 2 M NaOH at 80 °C, the ion conductivity only decreased by 10.32% and the tensile strength decreased by 11.05%. The peak power density of H2–O2 AEMFC based on PTFI-IZ-8 can reach 1.03 W/cm2 at 80 °C, providing a new strategy for the design of high-performance anion exchange membranes.

item.title: Hydrogen Adsorption on Alkali-Metal-Decorated g-SiC 5 Siligraphene: A First-Principles Study
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, density functional theory calculations were used to evaluate pristine and alkali-metal-decorated g-SiC5 as molecular hydrogen adsorbents. Pristine g-SiC5 is dynamically stable along the sampled phonon path but binds H2 weakly, with an adsorption energy of −0.136 eV. Li, Na, and K decoration creates positively polarized adsorption centers that strengthen H2 binding without dissociation. Among the single-metal systems, Li@g-SiC5 provides the most consistent combination of metal binding, compact metal–H2 geometry, and moderate average adsorption energies. Each Li center accommodates up to four H2 molecules in the optimized configuration. Increasing the Li coverage produces optimized 8H2@2Li@g-SiC5, 12H2@3Li@g-SiC5, and 16H2@4Li@g-SiC5 configurations with average adsorption energies of −0.28, −0.25, and −0.24 eV/H2 and theoretical gravimetric capacities of 4.22, 6.08, and 7.82 wt %, respectively. Charge-density-difference and reduced-density-gradient analyses support polarization-assisted physisorption. The AIMD simulations performed over 5 ps indicate substantial retention of the adsorbed H2 molecules at 77 K and partial release at 300 K, while the g-SiC5 framework remains structurally intact at both temperatures. The thermodynamic model predicts a strong dependence of H2 uptake on temperature and pressure. For the fully loaded system, the characteristic van’t Hoff temperature increases from 306.95 K at 1 bar to 422.72 K at 12 bar, while the grand canonical independent-site model predicts 3.09–5.84 H2 molecules per cell at 300 K and 5–12 bar. Thus, the 7.82 wt % capacity represents the maximum optimized loading rather than the equilibrium uptake under all operating conditions.

item.title: Water- and Alkali-Stable Cellulose Nanocrystal Films via Synergistic Citric Acid Cross-Linking and Poly(vinyl alcohol) Incorporation for Hydroxide-Conducting Membranes
item.description:
Abstract
Cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) are promising reinforcing materials for biopolymer films, but their poor stability in water and alkaline environments limits their application in alkaline energy-conversion systems. In this study, CNC-based composite films (CNC/CP) were fabricated through a simple aqueous suspension-casting method using citric acid (CA) as a green cross-linker and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA, 10 wt%) as a secondary polymer. The cross-linking degree was controlled by varying the CA content from 10 to 30 wt% relative to CNC, followed by heat treatment to promote esterification. The combined effect of CA cross-linking and PVA incorporation greatly improved the film performance. The CNC/CP films showed excellent water stability, with low swelling values of ∼6.66% and 20% after 960 h at room temperature and 80 °C. Mechanical performance was also improved, with the optimized CNC/CP film showing a 109.9% increase in tensile strength and a 590.3% increase in toughness compared with the pristine CNC film. The hydroxide-ion conductivities of CNC/CP films reached up to 122.64 mS cm–1 at 25 °C and 157.99 mS cm–1 at 80 °C in 1 M KOH. Moreover, the CNC/CP films showed good alkaline stability, retaining hydroxide-ion conductivities of 29.32–48.25 mS cm–1 after soaking in 1 M KOH for 720 h. These results show that citric acid cross-linking combined with PVA incorporation is an effective strategy to produce stable, mechanically robust, and conductive CNC-based films for further alkaline energy-conversion applications.

item.title: Wearable Organic Electrochemical Transistor Biosensor for Real-Time Measurement of Sweat Salinity and Saturation
item.description:
Abstract
Wearable sweat sensing offers a noninvasive strategy for continuous monitoring of hydration, electrolyte balance, and physiological stress. Here, we demonstrate a flexible textile-based organic electrochemical transistor (OECT) biosensor for real-time quantification of sweat salinity and saturation during physical activity. The device consists of cotton fibers functionalized with the conductive polymer PEDOT:PSS, configured as channel and gate electrodes within a biocompatible patch. The gate and drain currents measured by the device in response to sweat are decoded using a mathematical model that estimates both the total salt concentration and the sweat saturation level. Unlike conventional enzymatic or membrane-based sensors, the platform operates without selective coatings, improving robustness, reproducibility, and mechanical stability. In in vitro tests, the device exhibited a linear response in the 10–4 M–1 M concentration range, a limit of detection as low as 10-5 M, and a response time below 40 s. Moreover, the sensor device was validated in three participants during treadmill running sessions lasting up to 1 h. The saturation profiles derived from the sensor showed a very high correlation with facial skin temperature measured by infrared thermography in all participants (up to 0.90), and with heart rate variability (HRV) derived from ECG recordings in two of the three participants (up to 0.86). Cross-correlation analysis revealed that the time lag between the onset of the exercise-induced increase in body temperature and the onset of sweating ranges from 600 to 740 s, in line with values predicted by the literature. These results demonstrate accurate, sensitive, and continuous tracking of sweat dynamics in real time. The proposed wearable OECT platform establishes a robust foundation for biomedical applications including monitoring of hydration disorders, electrolyte imbalance, metabolic dysfunction, and autonomic dysregulation.

item.title: Radiolabeling and Preclinical Evaluation of [ 77 Br]hGTS13, an xCT-Targeted Small Molecule
item.description:
Abstract
