item.title: Nano-Boron Enhances Boron Accumulation and Alters the Tomato Leaf Metabolome: Molecular Modeling of Leaf-Surface and Boron Transporter–Metabolite Interactions
item.description:
Abstract
Boron (B) deficiency severely limits tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) productivity and fruit quality, particularly in alkaline or low-organic-matter soils, while conventional foliar boron fertilizers suffer from low uptake efficiency and environmental losses. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel nanoboron (NB) formulation and evaluated its efficacy compared with boric acid using physicochemical characterization, molecular simulations, greenhouse studies, metabolomics, and field validation. Physicochemical analyses confirmed stable nanoscale particles (∼58 nm hydrodynamic diameter, PDI 0.266, zeta potential −15.7 mV) with favorable colloidal stability. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable interfacial association of the nanoformulation with the leaf surface model without disruptive penetration. The foliar application in tomato cv. Shivam resulted in significantly higher boron accumulation in NB-treated leaves (1550–2080 ppm over 4–14 days) compared with boric acid and untreated controls. Untargeted metabolomics revealed distinct metabolic reprogramming, with significant modulation of stress-associated metabolites and volatile compounds following NB treatment. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions of differentially regulated metabolites with boron transporters (BOR1, NIP5;1) and antioxidant-related proteins, indicating possible links to boron homeostasis and redox regulation. Field-level validation demonstrated that NB significantly improved reproductive and yield parameters, including flower number, fruit set, fruit weight, and total yield (∼21 t ha–1), compared with conventional boric acid treatments. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the NB formulation is an effective and sustainable foliar boron delivery system with enhanced nutrient use efficiency and promising agronomic benefits for tomato cultivation.

item.title: A Pyrroloquinoline-Based Colchicine-Binding Site Inhibitor Drives Mitotic Arrest and Caspase-Dependent Apoptosis
item.description:
Abstract
Targeting the colchicine-binding site on tubulin represents a promising strategy for developing anticancer agents capable of overcoming drug resistance and alleviating limitations of current microtubule-targeting therapies. Building on the pharmacological potential of quinoline scaffolds, we designed pyrroloquinoline-based compounds aimed at targeting the colchicine-binding site on tubulin. A hypothesis-driven design strategy, guided by structure- and ligand-based molecular modeling, was employed to prioritize the designed molecules for strong predicted binding and pharmacophoric complementarity within the colchicine-binding site. A concise, efficient synthetic strategy was employed to access the target molecules, which were subsequently evaluated for antiproliferative activity across various cancer cell lines. The hit compounds reported in this paper, 4a and 5b, exhibited potent cytotoxicity, competitively inhibited the formation of the EBI−β-tubulin adduct, and induced pronounced disruption of the intracellular microtubule network. Compound 4a, in particular, consistently displayed significant biological activity, as mechanistic studies revealed that it triggers sustained G2/M phase arrest, suppresses proliferative signaling, and activates DNA damage–associated stress responses, followed by caspase-3 activation and PARP cleavage, indicative of caspase-dependent apoptosis. These results reinforce the utility of the quinoline scaffold for the development of colchicine-site microtubule inhibitors and highlight their potential in advancing new chemotherapeutic candidates.

item.title: Enhancing Response Surface Methodology for Bioprocesses Development Using Interpretable Machine Learning
item.description:
Abstract
Response surface methodology (RSM) has been a cornerstone for experimental bioprocess optimization, yet its reliance on polynomial equations often fails to capture complex nonlinearities and requires extensive experimental data to attempt capturing them. This study evaluates the enhancement of RSM through machine learning (ML) techniques, specifically Gaussian Processes and Support Vector Machines, across three biological systems: succinic acid fermentation, biobutanol production, and continuous ethanol cultivation. To mitigate the “black-box” nature of ML, explainability measures such as Mutual Information (MI) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) were integrated to assess feature importance and ensure biological relevance. Results demonstrate that ML models consistently outperform traditional polynomials in predictive accuracy, even when having access to less experimental data for calibration and a reduced space of features, particularly on validation data sets where errors were significantly reduced (e.g., reaching MAPE lower than 1% in simulated experimental scenarios). Furthermore, the application of Model-Based Design of Experiments using Latin Hypercube Designs achieved optimal conditions with up to 50% fewer experimental runs compared to traditional factorial approaches. These findings suggest that coupling ML with explainability tools improves the reliability of finding optimal conditions for bioprocess development while also significantly enhancing operational efficiency by reducing experimental runs, time, and costs.

item.title: Dynamic PET-Based Networks: A Critical Review of Reactive Strategies, Processing Windows, and Circular Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is an industrial commodity, with global production reaching ∼82 million metric tons in 2024 and a projected market value of USD 40.66 billion by 2025. Despite its ubiquity, PET circularity is hindered by thermomechanical degradation during recycling. This review addresses a significant gap by integrating chemical design, semicrystalline morphology, and industrial scalability. A comparison of recent developments reveals that while imine, disulfide, and boronic chemistries are widely researched, they fail in PET due to moisture sensitivity and thermal instability. Ester-based transesterification is established as the only mechanism intrinsically compatible with the PET backbone. A key highlight is that PET vitrimer behavior is morphology-limited rather than chemistry-limited. With crystallinity levels between 25% and 45%, exchange reactions are confined to the amorphous phase, resulting in heterogeneous stress relaxation and high activation energies. Furthermore, stress relaxation alone is an insufficient validation metric; molecular weight retention must be monitored to ensure flow originates from associative exchange rather than degradation. Regarding scalability, reactive extrusion (RE) is the primary industrial platform. Success depends on moisture management, defined as a first-order design variable to prevent hydrolysis within narrow processing windows. By balancing exchange kinetics against degradation, this work provides actionable principles for the scalable upcycling of PET into high-performance materials for a circular economy.

item.title: Deciphering the Material Basis of an Herbal Formula via Integrated Two-dimensional Chromatography, In Silico Screening, and Comparative Pharmacokinetics: A Case Study of Kaiyu Jiangzhuo Formula
item.description:
Abstract
Kaiyu Jiangzhuo (KYJZ) is a Chinese medicine formula composed of nine herbs. Its efficacy in alleviating glycolipid metabolic disorders and reducing the incidence of diabetes mellitus in overweight patients with prediabetes has been widely validated. Although our previous studies separately characterized the chemical constituents of the KYJZ decoction and the components detected in plasma, the relationship between chemical profiling and systemic exposure remains undefined. In particular, it is unclear which decoction constituents are absorbed into systemic circulation and how obesity modulates their pharmacokinetic profiles. This study aimed to comprehensively profile the components of KYJZ and identify potential bioactive constituents by integrating in silico screening, comparative pharmacokinetic, and tissue distribution studies. Two-dimensional liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (2D-LC–MS) and a hybrid method (data-dependent acquisition/high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring) were employed to decipher the chemical profile and circulating components of KYJZ, respectively. Components exhibiting high binding affinity for antiobesity targets (composite Z-score >0.4) were selected for further pharmacokinetic study. In summary, 316 compounds were identified in KYJZ using 2D-LC–MS/MS. Among these, 99 compounds were recognized as circulating constituents, and 16 with a composite Z-score >0.4 were specifically selected for comparative pharmacokinetic evaluation in mice fed a normal-chow diet (NCD) or a high-fat diet (HFD). Comparative pharmacokinetics revealed that long-term HFD feeding significantly changed the pharmacokinetic behavior of circulating components in mice, especially protoberberine-type alkaloids. Despite their low plasma exposure, they were detected at their highest concentrations in the liver relative to all other tissues examined, suggesting that the liver may represent a relevant organ contributing to the antiobesity effects of KYJZ. Our findings highlight the capability of two-dimensional chromatography to characterize complex herbal medicines and establish a novel analysis pipeline integrating chemical profiling, in silico screening, and comparative pharmacokinetic analysis for identifying bioactive components in traditional Chinese medicine formulas.

item.title: Toward Mild Conditions for N 2 Activation: Progress and Challenges from Nitrogenase to Biomimetic Artificial Catalysts
item.description:
Abstract
Nitrogen (N2), as the most abundant gas in the atmosphere, poses a long-standing challenge in chemistry and biochemistry due to its high bond energy (≈941 kJ·mol–1) and thus low reactivity under mild conditions. In nature, nitrogenase can reduce N2 to ammonia at ambient temperature and pressure, while industry relies on the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch process for ammonia synthesis. This paper systematically reviews the mechanisms and catalytic progress in biological nitrogen fixation and industrial ammonia synthesis, with a focus on the structure and catalytic mechanism of nitrogenase, as well as the catalytic mechanisms and green pathways for industrial ammonia production. It further summarizes the design strategies and recent advances in artificial nitrogen fixation catalysts inspired by nitrogenase. For example, a biomimetic iron–molybdenum dual-atom catalyst on carbonized delignified wood (FeMo-CDW) recently achieved an NH3 production rate of 336.03 μg·h–1·cm–2 under acidic conditions, while an Fe single-atom catalyst supported on monolayer MoS2 delivered an NH3 production rate of 97.5 ± 6 μg·h–1·cm–2, underscoring the practical promise of nitrogenase-inspired systems. By reviewing molecular catalysts, metal sulfides/carbides, single-atom catalysts, and related directions, this review paper outlines future development pathways for efficient nitrogen fixation catalytic systems under mild conditions, offering theoretical insights and design principles for breakthroughs in green ammonia synthesis technologies.

item.title: Plasma-Activated 3D-Printed Electrode for the Determination of Tolfenamic Acid in Environmental Samples
item.description:
Abstract
The occurrence of tolfenamic acid (TA) in aquatic environments has raised concerns regarding its potential environmental impacts, highlighting the need for rapid, sensitive, and low-cost analytical methods for its determination. In this work, a conductive CB/PLA filament was fabricated through a solvent-free thermal mixing approach and used to produce a 3D-printed electrochemical sensor for TA determination. This strategy provides a greener and scalable route for electrode fabrication. Atmospheric air plasma treatment was applied to improve the electrochemical performance of the CB/PLA electrode. SEM images revealed the partial removal of the insulating PLA matrix, increasing the exposure of the conductive carbon sites. This modification resulted in lower charge-transfer resistance (Rct from 33.4 to 7.6 kΩ). Under optimized differential pulse voltammetry conditions, the plasma-treated electrode (CB/PLA-PT) exhibited a linear response toward TA in the concentration range of 1.91–20.1 μmol L–1, with detection and quantification limits of 0.54 and 1.80 μmol L–1, respectively. The sensor demonstrated satisfactory precision (RSD ≤ 5.7%) and selectivity in the presence of common interfering species. Its applicability was successfully demonstrated in spiked river and tap water samples, yielding recovery values between 92 and 105%. The proposed approach combines 3D printing and reagent-free plasma activation to provide a simple and environmentally friendly platform for the electrochemical determination of TA in environmental waters.

item.title: Effect of the Applied Pressure on the Physical and Chemical Properties of Nickel Films Prepared by Electroless Plating on Beech Wood
item.description:
Abstract
Nickel films were deposited on beech wood substrates using the electroless plating method, and the effect of applied mechanical pressures (2, 4, 6, and 8 kN/cm2) on their structural, morphological, wetting, and electrical properties was systematically investigated. Nickel-coated wood specimens were subjected to uniaxial pressures for 3 s, followed by characterization using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), contact-angle (CA) measurements, and current–voltage (I–V) analysis. SEM revealed surface openings of approximately 2–4 μm at 2 kN/cm2, which progressively narrowed with increasing pressure and were nearly absent at 8 kN/cm2. Cross-sectional SEM-EDS confirmed Ni penetration into the porous wood structure, with the greatest apparent penetration depth observed at 6 kN/cm2. XRD identified face-centered-cubic Ni with a preferential (111) orientation, while Williamson-Hall analysis indicated pressure-dependent variations in crystallite size and lattice microstrain. The wetting behavior exhibited a pressure-dependent response, with the highest initial contact angle observed at 6 kN/cm2, followed by a decrease at 8 kN/cm2 consistent with increased water penetration associated with pressure-induced surface and interfacial damage. All samples exhibited approximately linear I–V characteristics (R2 > 0.99), with the highest electrical response observed at 6 kN/cm2 and a subsequent decline at 8 kN/cm2. Overall, the results demonstrate a pressure-dependent balance between compaction of the nickel conductive network at moderate pressures and mechanical degradation under excessive compression, providing a basis for pressure-controlled design of functional conductive Ni/wood interfaces.

item.title: Efficient Extraction and Recovery of Astaxanthin from Bacterial Sources Using Fatty Acids
item.description:
Abstract
Natural astaxanthin is heavily preferred over synthetic alternatives for both food and pharmaceutical applications due to its superior bioactivity. However, conventional recovery methods rely on toxic volatile organic solvents (VOCs) and energy-intensive thermal distillation. This study presents an integrated, nonthermal biorefining strategy for Paracoccus carotinifaciens using short- and medium-chain food-grade fatty acids. The proposed “one-pot” process utilizes the pH-controlled dissociation of these solvents to simultaneously extract and recover the ketocarotenoids in a single vessel. Propanoic acid achieved the highest relative initial extraction efficiency (∼100%), outperforming acetic (88%) and butanoic (83%) acids. Subsequent alkaline phase-shifting triggered a thermodynamic “dissolution-to-precipitation” switch, yielding quantitative recovery (>98%) of carotenoids from propanoic, butanoic, and hexanoic acid solutions. High-performance liquid chromatography suggested the preliminary structural preservation of a highly enriched fraction of astaxanthin, adonirubin, and canthaxanthin relative to the starting bacterial biomass. Furthermore, a conceptual proof of principle of solvent recovery was demonstrated with hexanoic acid, achieving 80% bulk solvent recovery strictly via phase separation. This methodology completely eliminates VOCs and inherently bypasses thermal degradation, offering a highly sustainable, scalable route for industrial microbial pigment production.

item.title: Evaluating the Environmental and Biological Safety of Phosphonium-Based Porous Liquid Systems
item.description:
Abstract
Porous liquids have emerged as a promising class of advanced materials that combine permanent porosity with fluidity. They are often proposed as “green” alternatives in separations and catalysis, although their biological safety remains underexplored. Here, we present a comprehensive evaluation of the toxicity of two representative porous liquid systems based on methyltriphenylphosphonium bromide ([P1Ph3][Br]) and trihexyltetradecylphosphonium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)amide ([P66614][NTf2]), combined with glycerol and ZIF-8, across a spectrum of biological models. Acute toxicity was assessed in microorganisms (Escherichia coli), aquatic organisms (Daphnia magna, Raphidocelis subcapitata, Artemia franciscana), plants (tomato and oat), and human dermal fibroblasts. While both materials exhibited low cytotoxicity toward human dermal fibroblasts (IC50 > 0.5 mM), notable toxicity emerged in aquatic organisms and bacteria, especially for aromatic [P1Ph3][Br]-based systems (EC50 = 1–10 mg dm–3). The studied multicomponent formulations disrupted microbial growth and inhibited germination even at low concentrations, revealing unexpected phytotoxicity. These contrasting outcomes (limited toxicity toward HDF cells, notable ecotoxicity) highlight the hidden complexity of structure-toxicity relationships in porous liquids. Our findings call for a shift from assumption to evidence in the development of so-called “green” solvents, as functionality must go hand in hand with environmental foresight.

item.title: Functionalization of Carbon Nanotubes with 5-Phenylvaleryl, Pentadecanoyl, and Adipoyl Chloride: Synthesis and Spectroscopic Surface Analysis Toward Biomarker Sensing
item.description:
Abstract
Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were covalently modified with aromatic (5-phenylvaleryl, 5PC), long-chain aliphatic (pentadecanoyl, PDC), and oxygen-rich/carboxylated (adipoyl, ACC) chemistries to create a tunable surface interface for detecting volatile and semivolatile chemical biomarkers. Following oxidative activation, 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) amination, and acyl-chloride coupling, successful attachment and differentiation of linker classes were evaluated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS), and C KLL Auger analysis. Distinct spectroscopic fingerprints corresponding to aromatic, aliphatic, and oxygenated functionalities were resolved despite the intrinsically carbon-rich substrate. These orthogonal signatures provide a compact quality-control strategy for CNT functionalization and establish a framework for correlating surface chemistry with predicted analyte interactions, including aromatic interactions, nonpolar adsorption, and acid–base or hydrogen-bond pairing. This surface chemistry palette is intended to enable flexible CNT-based sensor arrays for noninvasive monitoring of clinically relevant biomarkers, including ketones associated with diabetes, nitrogen-containing species linked to chronic kidney disease, and volatile compounds implicated in preictal seizure states. Sensor-level performance was not evaluated in the present study and is the subject of ongoing device work.

item.title: Lightguide–Lens Array Side–Absorption Concentrated Photovoltaic (CPV) System with an Extended Acceptance Angle
item.description:
Abstract
A lightguide–lens–array side-absorption concentrated photovoltaic system (LLA-SCPV) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated for wide-angle operation. The bottom surface of the lightguide is patterned with reflective V-grooves to direct incident light toward solar cells mounted on its sidewalls. Both the lightguide and the lens array are made of PMMA. The device exhibits a simulated acceptance angle of at least ±12° and an experimental acceptance angle of ±15°. Through an optical efficiency breakdown, manufacturing profile deviations and reduced reflectance of the V-groove facets are identified as the primary factors of the optical loss, while the V-groove profile deviations broaden the angular response. For further performance improvement, simulations under realistic industrial conditions indicate that replacing PMMA with fused silica, increasing V-groove reflectance to 0.86 and reducing the corner radius to 0.1 mm can enhance the optical efficiency to 67.7% while maintaining an acceptance angle of approximately ±15.5°.

item.title: Agnuside from Vitex negundo L. Attenuates Hepatocellular Lipid Accumulation: Association with the AMPK/SREBP1/FASN/HMGCR/PPARα/UCP2 Signaling Network
item.description:
Abstract
Vitex negundo L. (VN) is a medicinal plant known for its anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties, commonly used as a vegetable in northeastern Indian communities. However, its role in treating nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is still underexplored. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of VN and its bioactive compounds in reducing lipid accumulation in CC1 hepatocytes. A crude extract of VN and its n-butanol fraction (VNBU) were tested on palmitate-induced CC1 hepatocytes to evaluate lipid accumulation. Key compounds Agnuside, 5-hydroxy-3,6,7,3́,4́-pentamethoxyflavone, and Vitexilactone were isolated. Agnuside’s effects on lipogenesis, cholesterol accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation were assessed using biochemical assays and Western blot analysis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to explore its interactions with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR). Agnuside treatment was associated with reduced lipid accumulation by modulating Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), HMGCR, Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBP1), Fatty acid synthase (FASN), Peroxisome Proliferator-activated receptors (PPARα), and uncoupling protein (UCP2), suggesting a favorable shift in lipid metabolism. Computational studies indicated that Agnuside binds stably to HMGCR, similar to statins. In summary, these findings suggest that VN and Agnuside exert protective effects in hepatocytes, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism markers. Further studies are needed to confirm the causal role of this signaling network.

item.title: Thermochemistry of the Water Splitter SrTi 0.5 Mn 0.5 O 3−δ Studied Using Density Functional Theory (DFT+ U )
item.description:
Abstract
SrTi0.5Mn0.5O3 (STM55) perovskite has been proven experimentally to be a promising material for hydrogen production using thermochemical water splitting. However, optimizing the performance of STM55 in this application requires a synergistic study of its thermochemical properties using both experiments and computations. In particular, there are several questions with regard to its crystal structure, magnetic ordering, electronic structure, and, more importantly, its off-stoichiometry variation as a function of temperature and oxygen chemical potential. Herein, we tackle these questions employing density functional theory calculations equipped with onsite Hubbard (U) terms applied to Mn and Ti 3d states. This study revealed that STM55 behaves electronically as a metal and is best modeled as a ferromagnet in the pm-3m crystal structure. Oxygen vacancy creation is controlled by the Mn4+/Mn3+ redox couple with minor intervention from Ti cations. Upon a thorough analysis, we selected a set of U parameters (UMn = 3 eV and UTi = 5 eV) that reasonably predict the oxide thermodynamic stability, the oxide off-stoichiometry variations with temperature and oxygen partial pressure, and the temperature dependence of the enthalpy of reduction in the dilute defect regime. Our work furnishes grounds for future extension of our predictive thermodynamic modeling to the nondilute regime by including defect–defect interactions and has general implications for the thermochemistry of the class of metallic oxides.

item.title: An Enzymatic Step toward the Energetic Material CL-20 via Laccase-Mediated Oxidation of HBIW to TADBIW (Hexabenzylhexaazaisowurtzitane to Tetraacetyldibenzylhexaazaisowurtzitane)
item.description:
Abstract
The synthesis of one of the most powerful non-nuclear energetics, CL-20 (HNIW; 2,4,6,8,10,12-hexanitro-2,4,6,8,10,12-hexaazaisowurtzitane) requires a step that debenzylates the intermediate HBIW (hexabenzylhexaazaisowurtzitane) to TADBIW (tetraacetyldibenzylhexaazaisowurtzitane). In current chemical processes, this transformation requires a palladium catalyst, which is challenging to source and recycle on the industrial scale. Here, we characterize a laccase enzyme in combination with a chemical oxidant to catalyze this step. A commercial Trametes versicolor laccase is tested for its ability to oxidize mediators that, in turn, facilitate the debenzylation of HBIW to form the intermediate DBIW (dibenzylhexaazaisowurtzitane). This intermediate is unstable and is acetylated to TADBIW. We screen six mediators for this reaction and find that ABTS (2,2′-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid)) is the most efficient mediator. Critically, ABTS generates TADBIW only in the presence of the laccase, at yields of 1.0%, compared to yields of 3.4% from the potassium permanganate positive control alone. High-resolution tandem mass spectrometry supports TADBIW identification, placing both benzyl and acetyl groups on a retained isowurtzitane cage. This work demonstrates the substitution of an inorganic process for a lower-cost, more-sustainable enzymatic one towards an alternative pathway to CL-20.

item.title: A Basic Matrix Protein Songin Selectively Promotes Aragonite Aggregation and Modulates Calcium Carbonate Crystallization in Hyriopsis cumingii
item.description:
Abstract
In China, the pearl industry of Hyriopsis cumingii contributes approximately 80% of pearl production. Matrix proteins play crucial roles in shell and pearl biomineralization. However, the functions of basic matrix proteins in H. cumingii remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified a novel predicted secreted basic matrix protein, designated Songin, from the freshwater pearl mussel H. cumingii. Functional assays were performed using a chemically synthesized 53-amino-acid peptide corresponding to the predicted mature region of Songin. Songin transcripts showed a relative mantle-enriched expression pattern and were detected in dorsal mantle epithelial cells, suggesting a potential association with shell biomineralization. In the end point crystallization assay, Songin was associated with pronounced aggregation of mineral particles under Mg2+-containing aragonite-favoring conditions while exerting only minor effects on particle morphology in the calcite-favoring system. Raman spectroscopy supported the predominant polymorph assignments in the calcite-favoring and Mg2+-containing aragonite-favoring systems, and no obvious Songin-associated change in the predominant polymorph was detected under the tested conditions. Laser scanning confocal microscopy showed heterogeneous Cy5-associated fluorescence near localized regions of some mineral particles. Because free Cy5 and Cy5-labeled BSA controls were not included, nonspecific dye adsorption cannot be excluded, and these observations are regarded as preliminary qualitative information rather than evidence of specific crystal-surface binding. This study indicates that the synthetic mature-region Songin peptide was associated with pronounced mineral-particle aggregation under Mg2+-containing aragonite-favoring conditions in vitro, suggesting a potential role in mineral-particle assembly during shell biomineralization. These findings provide preliminary insight into the possible involvement of Songin in shell biomineralization.

item.title: Sustainable Self-Healing Thermoresponsive Nanocomposite Derived from Shrimp Shells and Lignin Biowaste for Water Shutoff in Ultradeep High-Temperature, High-Salinity Carbonate Reservoirs
item.description:
Abstract
Excessive water production in ultradeep, extreme high-temperature and high-salinity (HTHS) carbonate reservoirs has emerged as a major challenge, reducing hydrocarbon productivity and creating substantial environmental and economic burdens. Herein, we report, for the first time, the synthesis of a novel, highly resilient, sustainable, self-healing, thermoresponsive chitin-based nanocomposite hydrogel for water shutoff, specifically tailored to endure extreme harsh conditions of 160 °C and 350,000 ppm salinity. The nanocomposite was synthesized via a near-zero-waste approach utilizing chitin and CaCO3 nanoparticles derived from shrimp shell biomass, employing a recyclable, CO2-switchable natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES)-assisted enzymatic process. The extracted chitin was copolymerized with vinyl ester sulfonated lignin (VESL), a green macromonomer derived from industrial lignin waste, and 1-vinylimidazole (VIm) via free radical polymerization. The hydrogel composition has been optimized using response surface methodology (RSM) with central composite design. The nanocomposite was thoroughly characterized by FTIR, 1H NMR, SEM, EDX, TGA, and DTG analysis. The optimized nanocomposite demonstrated a superior swelling ratio and viscoelastic properties even at an ultralow polymer concentration of 0.08 wt % across temperatures of 25 to 160 °C and salinities up to 350,000 ppm. Core-flooding experiments indicated effective fracture plugging with high RRF values of 300.5 ± 5.7 and 191.1 ± 4.8 (with plugging efficiencies of 99.7 ± 0.4% and 99.5 ± 0.5%, respectively) using ultralow nanocomposite concentrations of 0.08 wt % and 0.1 wt %, respectively. This research presents a sustainable strategy that integrates the CO2-switchable green extraction of chitin with lignin for valorization of marine and industrial biowaste into a high-performance self-healing hydrogel for water shutoff in ultra-HTHS reservoirs.

item.title: Pore-Scale Remaining Oil Characterization by Integrated Online NMR and Micro-CT
item.description:
Abstract
An integrated online nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and microcomputed tomography (micro-CT) workflow was established to characterize remaining oil mobilization in water-flooded heavy-oil porous media at the pore scale. NMR enabled quantitative tracking of oil-phase depletion across distinct pore-throat intervals via a transverse relaxation time (T2)–pore-throat radius conversion relationship, while micro-CT provided direct spatial and morphological identification of remaining oil. For the investigated cores, the power-law calibration provided better agreement with the mercury-intrusion pore-throat distributions than the linear counterpart. Core permeability, oil viscosity, and displacement velocity collectively govern the extent and location of remaining oil mobilization. With increasing permeability, the dominant mobilized pore-throat interval shifts from small–medium throats, 1–20 μm, to medium–large throats, 20–40 μm and above. CT-derived oil displacement efficiencies showed trends generally consistent with the NMR-based evaluation and further revealed that extended high-pore-volume water flooding and late-stage flow acceleration could still mobilize a portion of the remaining oil, albeit with diminishing incremental recovery. This integrated approach bridges the gap between pore-size-resolved quantification and three-dimensional spatial evidence, offering a robust framework for evaluating remaining-oil potential after prolonged water flooding in heavy-oil reservoirs.

item.title: Proteasome Inhibitor MG132 Facilitates Antiviral Effects by Inhibiting TFEB Degradation and Activating Autophagy
item.description:
Abstract
The ubiquitin-proteasome system, which serves as one of the most common cellular degradation pathways, plays a critical role in maintaining proteostasis. Yet, the correlation between the ubiquitin-proteasome system and antiviral defense remains to be defined. In this work, pharmacological inhibition of proteasomes via treatment with MG132, which inhibited proteasome activity during viral infection, facilitated antiviral effects in vitro. Similar to MG132, another proteasome inhibitor, bortezomib, effectively inhibited proteasome activity and exhibited antiviral effects. Guided by these findings, further assays demonstrated that MG132 blocked viral adsorption and internalization, which partially contributed to the antiviral effects. Meanwhile, MG132 inhibited TFEB degradation and promoted dephosphorylation of TFEB at Ser211, resulting in autophagy, which was associated with antiviral effects. Taken together, a key discovery of our study is the critical role of the proteasome inhibitor MG132 in promoting antiviral activity, providing valuable insights for the development of more effective antiviral strategies based on the autophagy signaling pathway mediated by TFEB.

item.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Solid-State Nanopore Analysis for Single-Molecule Discrimination of Albumin and Aptamer-Bound Glycated Albumin Complexes
item.description:
Abstract
Discriminating glycated human serum albumin from unmodified albumin and aptamer-bound complexes at the single-molecule level is a sensing challenge unmet by conventional bulk analytical methods, which cannot resolve individual protein modification states. Here, we present a proof-of-concept solid-state nanopore platform combined with aptamer recognition and supervised machine learning for single-event discrimination of human serum albumin (HSA), glycated HSA (GHSA), and aptamer-bound GHSA (Apt+GHSA). Using a 14 nm silicon nitride nanopore, synthetic HSA, GHSA, and Apt+GHSA produced distinguishable ionic current blockade signatures, while dwell times remained similar. Serum-derived HSA showed broader, heterogeneous blockade distributions consistent with mixed albumin proteoforms; aptamer treatment generated a higher-blockade population consistent with Apt+GHSA-like events. A modified fluorescence aptamer assay estimated serum glycated albumin content at approximately 30%. To resolve overlapping signatures, five signal-derived features were extracted from individual translocation events and used to train supervised machine learning classifiers. Random Forest and Gradient Boosting achieved the highest three-class test accuracy of 94.50% for HSA, Apt+GHSA, and serum-derived HSA; Gradient Boosting achieved the highest macroaverage AUC of 0.9915. Applied to aptamer-treated serum-derived HSA, Gradient Boosting classified 54.6% of events as Apt+GHSA-like, reflecting aptamer-responsive nanopore signatures rather than a direct quantification of the glycated albumin percentage. This study establishes a nanopore–aptamer–machine learning framework for resolving albumin modification and binding states in biologically derived samples.

item.title: Crystallinity-Regulated Hydration, Molecular Mobility, and Mechanical Softening of Poly(ether ether ketone): A Reactive Molecular Dynamics Study
item.description:
Abstract
Poly(ether ether ketone) (PEEK) is a high-performance semicrystalline thermoplastic widely used in aerospace, biomedical, and energy applications because of its excellent mechanical properties and resistance to harsh environments. However, the molecular mechanisms governing its short-time response to moisture exposure remain incompletely understood. In this work, reactive molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the short-time hydration response of amorphous and semicrystalline PEEK in the dry state and at 1 and 3 wt % water. Water distribution, local hydration structure, molecular mobility, density-derived glass-transition behavior, and constrained directional moduli were analyzed to establish relationships among crystallinity, hydration, and thermomechanical behavior. Water showed greater local association with carbonyl oxygen than with ether oxygen, while increasing water content increased local coordination and molecular fluctuations. In semicrystalline PEEK, crystalline domains spatially confined these hydration-induced mobility enhancements, whereas the density-derived apparent glass-transition temperature showed a modest downward trend at 3 wt % water that was not resolved within the observed simulation variability. Increasing water content nevertheless progressively reduced the constrained directional moduli through plasticization, particularly within the amorphous and crystal–amorphous interfacial regions, whereas the crystalline phase retained substantial chain-direction stiffness. These results indicate that within the constructed models and sampled time scale, crystalline morphology restricted hydration-induced plasticization by limiting water accessibility and molecular mobility. No persistent hydration-induced bond-cleavage events were observed over the simulated time scale.

item.title: Valorization of Rice Husk through the Development of New Materials of Silica Functionalized with Phthaloyl Diamide Ligands: Characterization, Isomer Effect, Ag + Adsorption Investigation, and Antibacterial Activity
item.description:
Abstract
Silica was obtained from rice husk, a low-cost and abundant agricultural waste, and chemically modified with three phthaloyl diamide ligand isomers, aiming to develop new materials with adsorptive and antibacterial potential. The prepared adsorbents were fully characterized, confirming the successful functionalization. The isomeric structure of the ligands significantly influenced both the uniformity and extent of functionalization and the Ag+ adsorption efficiency. The Ag+ adsorption was favored at pH 5.0 and room temperature, and the adsorption rate was very fast, reaching equilibrium in about 15 min. The maximum adsorption capacity was 19.94 mg g–1. Antibacterial tests demonstrated that the Ag+-loaded adsorbent exhibited marked antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, highlighting the dual functionality of the synthesized material. These results underscore the potential of phthaloyl-modified rice husk-derived silica as a novel and effective material for integrated Ag+ removal and antibacterial protection.

item.title: Rapid Point-of-Care Quantification of Urinary Tract Infection Biomarker Xanthine Oxidase
item.description:
Abstract
Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health threat. Overuse of antimicrobial drugs is a main driver of resistance, with urinary tract infections (UTIs) a common indication for antibiotic use. To improve UTI treatment and reduce antimicrobial resistance, real-time diagnostic tools for monitoring the host immune response are needed. Xanthine oxidase (XO) is an enzyme that is elevated in UTIs and shows potential for sensitive and selective detection of infection. We developed a rapid and sensitive point-of-care electrochemical sensor for XO detection by using a simple manufacturing approach. The sensor consists of a disposable carbon electrode embedded in a capillary fill chamber designed for point-of-care sample collection. After urine collection, XO catalyzes its substrate while changing the oxidation state of a secondary electron acceptor. The magnitude and rate of this redox shift reflects XO activity, enabling quantification of XO in urine. We demonstrate minimal intersensor variability of less than 5%, resulting in a calibration with an R2 of 0.985 across eight individual sensors. The capillary fill device was optimized to enable efficient substrate dissolution, reducing the time to result from 10 min to just 2 min. This approach enables calibration-free detection of XO in artificial and spiked human urine samples within 2 min of sample collection in both artificial urine and spiked human urine samples.

item.title: Straightforward Synthesis of Superparamagnetic Fe 3 O 4 -Carbon Dot Nanohybrids for Environmental Remediation: A Model Study Using Congo Red
item.description:
Abstract
Carbon dots (CDs) have attracted increasing interest as carbon-based nanomaterials due to their tunable surface chemistry, colloidal stability and low toxicity. Among them, magnetic carbon dots (MCDs) constitute a promising multifunctional subclass. In this work, magnetite-based magnetic carbon dots (Fe3O4-MCDs) were synthesized through a straightforward route using only ammonium ferric citrate and ethylenediamine as precursors. TEM revealed quasi-spherical Fe3O4-MCD nanohybrids with an average particle size of 12 ± 3 nm. XPS depth profiling employing Ar+ ion sputtering showed that these nanoparticles possess a magnetite-rich interior and a functionalized carbon-rich outer region. Furthermore, these nanoparticles self-assembled into hierarchical architectures with interparticle voids, resulting in a porous network with a specific surface area of 107 m2 g–1 and a pore volume of 0.431 cm3 g–1. In addition, the negligible coercivity and remanence are consistent with superparamagnetic-like behavior at room temperature, with a saturation magnetization of ∼60 emu g–1, facilitating rapid magnetic separation and redispersion. The Fe3O4-MCDs were evaluated for the adsorption of Congo red as a model pollutant, achieving an adsorption capacity of 121.6 mg g–1. Nonlinear kinetic analysis showed that adsorption followed the mixed 1,2-order model, while the Sips isotherm best described the equilibrium data. Overall, the results demonstrate that the Fe3O4-MCDs combine straightforward synthesis, high saturation magnetization, superparamagnetic behavior, and pollutant adsorption performance. These properties arise from their carbon/magnetite nanoarchitecture and engineered interfacial chemistry, promoting interactions with pollutants and highlighting their potential for multifunctional contaminant removal.

item.title: Reconsidering Catechol Contributions in Quantitative 31 P NMR Analyses of Lignins
item.description:
Abstract
Quantitative 31P NMR spectroscopy is widely used to determine phenolic hydroxyl group contents in lignins, yet the contribution of catechol functionalities is generally ambiguous. Using a series of catechol-containing lignin model compounds, we demonstrate that phosphitylated catechol hydroxyl groups yield signals that overlap extensively with conventional guaiacyl and syringyl regions and cannot be reliably distinguished by quantitative 31P NMR spectroscopy. Similar results were obtained by aromatic 1H–13C HSQC correlations under standard conditions. To address this limitation, we developed a complementary methodology combining quantitative 31P NMR with a semiquantitative chelometric/UV–vis determination of catechol groups. Application to technical (kraft and organosolv) and analytical (milled wood and enzymatic) grade lignins from softwoods, hardwoods, and grasses revealed measurable catechol contents in all samples examined and indicated that catechol functionalities accounted for approximately 6–27% of the phenolic hydroxyl content conventionally assigned to guaiacyl units, especially, in technical and modified lignins. Additionally, model-compound data further revealed that 5-methoxy-catechyl structures can contribute to the region conventionally assigned to syringyl phenolic hydroxyls. Taken together, our results suggest that conventional 31P NMR assignments may overestimate guaiacyl and syringyl hydroxyls in lignins containing catechol groups.

item.title: Effects of Methyl-Substituted Aniline Derivatives on Phase-Separated Bisphenol A-Based-Polybenzoxazine/Polyurethane Two-Way Shape Memory Polymers Behaviors
item.description:
Abstract
Two-way shape memory polymers (2WSMPs) based on gradient bilayer interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) architectures have attracted increasing attention owing to their ability to undergo reversible actuation without external reprogramming, making them promising candidates for applications such as self-folding structures, soft robotics, and safety circuit breakers. However, the molecular and morphological factors governing gradient architecture formation and their influence on reversible actuation behavior remain insufficiently explored. In this work, gradient bilayer IPNs were constructed in bisphenol A-based polybenzoxazine/polyurethane thermosetting systems by tailoring the benzoxazine phase using aromatic amines with different substitution patterns. A clear correlation between curing kinetics, cross-link density, phase morphology, and reversible actuation behavior was established. Meta-substituted systems (BA-3,5x and BA-mt) exhibited lower ring-opening polymerization temperatures, promoting early stage network formation and phase fixation during curing. The resulting higher cross-link density facilitated the formation of homogeneous benzoxazine-rich domains and distinct gradient bilayer architectures, as confirmed by FTIR, surface hardness, and AFM analyses. In contrast, ortho- and para-substituted systems (BA-ot and BA-pt) showed higher curing temperatures, lower network rigidity, and greater phase heterogeneity, resulting in poorly developed gradient architectures and insufficient structural integrity for reliable actuation. The optimized systems (BA-3,5x/PU and BA-mt/PU) demonstrated excellent reversible deformation, with high shape fixity (∼98%) and shape recovery (∼97–98%). Notably, BA-3,5x/PU exhibited faster recovery behavior (32–38 s) than BA-mt/PU (40–43 s), attributed to its higher cross-link density and more effective gradient bilayer architecture. This study provides correlation insights into gradient bilayer IPN formation and establishes a molecular design strategy for advanced two-way shape memory polymers.

item.title: Cryptococcus deuterogattii Lung Infection Leads to a Prothrombotic State Revealed by Proteomics and Functional Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Cryptococcosis caused by Cryptococcus deuterogattii is a life-threatening fungal infection increasingly reported in immunocompetent individuals. Although clinical evidence suggests that invasive fungal diseases could impact coagulation, the molecular mechanisms linking cryptococcal infection to hemostatic dysregulation remain unexplored. In this study, we employed an integrative approach combining in vivo rat lung infection model, proteomics, and in vitro assays to investigate alterations in coagulation and hemostasis induced by C. deuterogattii R265. Morphological and histological evaluations revealed progressive lung damage and cryptococcoma formation. Functional assays showed early thrombocytopenia, increased thrombin activity, reduced prothrombin time, and enhanced platelet aggregation, indicating a procoagulant state in the infection. Proteomic analysis identified the upregulation of platelet activation pathways and key prothrombotic proteins at 3 days post-inoculation (dpi), along with downregulation of anticoagulant regulators such as thrombomodulin and antithrombin III. At 14 dpi, a widespread protein downregulation suggests systemic collapse of host functions. Data are available via ProteomeXchange with identifier PXD077765. Coculture of A7R5 cells with C. deuterogattii confirmed increased tissue factor expression, reinforcing the role of the fungus in triggering thrombo-inflammatory responses and validating proteomics data. Our results provide the first molecular evidence linking cryptococcal infection to a dysregulated hemostatic profile, shedding light on host–pathogen interaction and suggesting that targeting coagulation pathways may offer novel therapeutic avenues in cryptococcosis management.

item.title: Synthesis and Biological Activity of Iminophosphine Copper(I) Complexes Derived from 2-(Diphenylphosphino)benzaldehyde and 4-Substituted-Benzylamines
item.description:
Abstract
A panel of copper(I) complexes was isolated by metal-templated reactions starting from 2-(diphenylphosphino)benzaldehyde and some 4-substituted-benzylamines, and by changing the ratio between metal and ligand and the anion. The spectroscopic characterization of the copper(I) complexes was completed by discussion of some structures obtained by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The copper(I) complexes were assayed in vitro against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923, Escherichia coli ATCC 25922, and Candida albicans ATCC 10231. Cell viability was assessed both in nonmalignant and malignant cell lines, namely Vero and Caco-2 cells, respectively. While the tested compounds show only a nonspecific antibacterial effect against S. aureus, some of them showed an interesting antiproliferative activity.
